“From the pendant, gather the things I need to act on from Mail, Calendar, GitHub, and my currently open private browser tabs; turn each into a sourced action card, create any reversible reminders or drafts, and keep working if I walk away.”
“Use my private apps and logged-in sites to complete this task, but don’t send the underlying private text to the cloud—just return the minimum facts and a preview of what would happen.”

“Prepare this across my logged-in browser and Mac, then ask me on the pendant to approve it. After I press once, do it only during a short lease, verify the result from the source, and tell me exactly what changed.”
“Cancel everything you’re waiting to do right now.”

“Carry out this decision everywhere it applies, and tell me exactly what changed.” For example: update the calendar event, send the approved browser reply, and save the final document on my Mac as one coordinated operation.
“If the app or website changes while you’re doing it, recover and finish the approved task without making me start over.”
“Do this, but only if the right account, page, and conditions are still true; ask me on the pendant at the last safe moment, then prove it actually happened.”
“Don’t just do it—tell me when it is independently witnessed as done, and tell me immediately if the witnesses disagree.”

Finish this across my Mac and logged-in browser tabs—even if I leave: carry out the dependent steps, resume after a device or network drops, and tell me exactly which steps happened, which did not, and what was undone.

Watch for the exact condition I described, and then carry out the whole prepared action automatically—for example, when the authenticated portal shows the approved invoice and the Mac is online, download it, file it, and tell me; do not act while any precondition is false.
When I tell the pendant to do something on my Mac, give me a physical completion signal, speak the exact result, and let me press once to undo the last reversible action.

When I say “I’m leaving,” check the unfinished work across my Mac, browser, and relay, tell me what is still exposed or running, and—only for the safe items I approve—close or hand them off so I can walk away with a spoken all-clear.
“Do this across my Mac and browser, and keep going if one step fails—tell me exactly what completed, what did not, and safely undo whatever can be undone.”
“After you do it, verify that the real-world result actually happened—not just that the click or command succeeded—and tell me if it didn’t.”

Do this across my Mac and logged-in browser, but only carry out steps that are still valid; stop at any irreversible step and show me exactly what would happen, then tell me what completed and what remains.

Hold this consequential task until I am physically present, then ask for one button press on the pendant and finish it across my logged-in browser and Mac; if the deadline passes or anything changes, stop and tell me exactly what remains.

“Prepare this booking or purchase, show me the exact final change, and only carry it through once I approve—if the browser or Mac disconnects, recover safely and tell me whether it actually completed.”
“When I’m physically with my Mac, let me authorize a sensitive action by pressing the pendant, and make the browser or Mac accept it only while that short-lived presence proof is valid.”
“Carry this out across my Mac and logged-in browser, but if anything changes underneath you, pause safely, keep my place, and tell me exactly what completed and what remains.”
“Stop whatever you’re doing everywhere.” (or double-press the pendant button)
“Handle this form using my logged-in information, but keep sensitive fields on my devices—do not send passwords, payment numbers, or identity numbers to the model or relay.”

“Hand this off to Alex.” From the pendant, create a safe, time-limited handoff packet containing the exact goal, relevant files or links from my Mac and logged-in browser, current status, and the one decision Alex needs to make; show me the packet before sharing, then let me revoke it or see whether Alex accepted it.

“Finish the prepared action.” The system should show me the exact pending changes in a short spoken summary, let me approve from the pendant, carry out the browser and Mac steps in order, survive a dropped voice connection, and later tell me exactly which side effects happened (or safely reconcile and stop).

“Keep this situation under control until it is resolved.” The system should monitor the outcome of a decision across my logged-in browser and Mac, detect an exception, choose the next permitted reversible step, and escalate to my pendant only when judgment is needed—for example, track a support case or delivery, prepare the next response when the status changes, and stop before any irreversible action.
“Before my next call, verify that my pendant audio is healthy; if it is not, fix what you can and tell me exactly what failed.”
“After you do it, prove that it actually happened—check the resulting app, page, or device state, and tell me if the proof is missing or contradicts the plan.”
“If this becomes urgent, keep trying every way to reach me until I acknowledge it—and show me when and where I acknowledged it.”

Make this change across my Mac and logged-in sites, and keep working until you can prove the final state is correct; if one step fails, tell me exactly what remains and safely repair only the reversible parts.
If this exact situation occurs, carry out the approved action automatically—but only while the facts I approved are still true, and tell me if the situation changed instead of using stale permission.
“Carry this through everywhere: update the source on my Mac, reflect it in the logged-in site, and tell me only when all sides agree it is done.”
“Stop everything right now.”
“Do it, and don’t tell me it’s done until you’ve verified the result.”
“Do this for me, but only if the world still matches what we agreed; tell me exactly what changed, and stop safely if anything is different.”
“When I walk away from my Mac, put my private work into a safe state; when I come back, restore exactly what I was doing.”
“If I hold the pendant button, revoke this device and stop anything acting as me everywhere.”

“Handle this end to end, and keep me in control.” The system should carry out a reversible multi-step task across my logged-in browser and Mac, pause only at irreversible steps, and let me approve, cancel, or resume it from the pendant.
“Do this wherever it can actually be done; if one device is unavailable, continue with the safe parts and tell me exactly what remains.”
“If this cannot be done now, keep it alive until the deadline, retry only when the missing device or account becomes available, and tell me before the deadline if it still cannot be finished.”
If the pendant's reply was clipped, garbled, or interrupted, say “repeat that” or press the button once and have the system resend only the missing part, then report whether recovery succeeded.

When I tell the pendant “finish this when I’m at my Mac,” have it preserve the exact spoken intent, wait until my Mac and browser session are both present, complete the reversible parts, and leave me a proof-backed review packet instead of making me repeat myself.

If the browser bridge is unavailable, check my currently open logged-in Safari tabs anyway, gather the requested facts, and tell me clearly whether anything could not be verified; never submit or change anything through the fallback.

Let me approve one real-world outcome once, then have the pendant, relay, Mac, and browser carry it through as one coordinated transaction: each surface reports its precondition and postcondition, the next step cannot run until the previous one is evidenced, and if I walk away or a device drops, it resumes safely without repeating completed side effects.

“If I tell you to do something while I’m away, queue it safely, carry it out when the right device comes back, and tell me whether the intended result actually happened—not merely whether a command ran.”
“Pause that job here and let me resume it from the exact next step on whichever device is available, with a compact explanation of what already happened and what will happen next.”
“I’m leaving now—carry out the prepared departure packet, but stop and tell me if anything no longer matches.”
“If this changes while I’m away, carry out the fallback I approved—within these limits—and tell me exactly what you did.”
Start this job now, but make it safe if I disconnect: pause before any irreversible step, tell me exactly what completed, and resume only after reconciling the Mac/browser state when I return.

Prepare the real-world change on my Mac or in my logged-in browser, then send me a compact exact summary on the pendant so I can approve that specific change from wherever I am; apply it only if the approved summary still matches, otherwise stop.

When I say 'check Gmail, GitHub, or my calendar' from the pendant, capture it even if my Mac or browser is offline, then resume automatically when they reconnect and give me a sourced spoken result; never send, edit, or delete anything without my confirmation.

When I say “get this ready for me,” let the pendant capture the request, have the Mac and my open browser determine the relevant document, messages, calendar constraints, and files, then assemble a private ready-to-review packet on the Mac and announce exactly what is missing—without sending, submitting, or changing anything.
Make sure that happened, and tell me if it didn't.
When I tell you to do something later, do it when I am actually at the right place and device—not merely at a clock time—and tell me if the opportunity passed.
“Start this on my Mac, and if it needs my approval while I’m away, ask me on the pendant; when I confirm, continue and tell me exactly what happened.”
“If this task gets stuck while I’m away, follow my fallback rules: save a draft, notify me, or cancel—whichever I specified—and never leave a half-finished change.”
Prepare this on my Mac and logged-in browser, then ask me on the pendant to confirm; only after I press the button should you commit it, and tell me exactly what happened.

After you do something for me, verify that the intended real-world result actually happened—not merely that the command returned success—and tell me if the outcome is confirmed, disproved, or still unknown.

When you do something for me, don't just say it was sent—keep working until the result is independently verified, tell me what actually changed on my pendant, and recover or ask me if it did not complete.
If I (or another device) change something while you are working on it, notice the conflict, show me both versions, and continue from the one I choose—never overwrite my newer change.

When I ask “did that happen?”, give me a proof-backed answer across my Mac, browser, relay, and pendant—what was only queued, what executed, what was delivered, and what cannot be verified—then offer the safest next step.

Before you carry out a consequential request, show me the likely cross-device state change; afterward, show me the actual state delta attributable to this action, including unexpected side effects, without relying on the app's claim that it succeeded.

“Do this for me, and keep going until you can prove whether it actually happened.” The pendant should capture my intent, the judgement agent should turn it into a bounded action bundle, the Mac or private browser should execute it, and perception should independently verify the resulting state before telling me it is done.

“Before you send or change anything irreversible, make sure the final target still matches what I originally meant—even if the task crossed apps or took an hour.” The system should detect semantic drift in recipient, amount, account, attachment, destination, or scope across the pendant, relay, Mac, and browser, and interrupt only when the final operation differs materially from the owner’s captured intent.
If something I asked you to do partly fails, recover it safely: show me what actually changed, undo the reversible parts when possible, and continue only after asking about the one blocked step.

Give me an emergency stop for anything you are doing on my Mac or in my browser: when I press and hold the pendant button, stop new actions immediately, cancel queued work, and tell me whether anything was already changed.

After I approve an action, carry it out across my devices and tell me whether it actually happened—not merely that a command was sent. If a device goes offline, keep the action safe, resume when it returns, and show me the evidence or the exact point where it stopped.

Give you a bounded standing permission for a kind of task—such as scheduling meetings within my working hours or reordering a specific item below a price cap—and have you carry out matching actions across my Mac and logged-in browser without asking me every time, while stopping and asking when any limit, ambiguity, or sensitive field is encountered.

“Do this wherever it can actually be done, and tell me whether it really happened.” For example: send the prepared message, update the appointment, or submit the form—even if I leave the pendant conversation.

“If part of this multi-step task fails, finish it safely or tell me exactly what is left—not just that the job failed.” For example, reschedule an appointment across my calendar and a logged-in portal, then notify the right person without duplicating or losing any step.
“Is my pendant audio path healthy? If not, diagnose it, switch to the safest working mode, and leave me a short report.”
“Make my pendant audio sound right wherever I am: run a quiet calibration, compensate for the bridge and headphones, and keep the correction until the hardware changes.”

When you have prepared something that needs my approval, say what will happen, then let me approve it with one deliberate long press on the pendant; execute it on my Mac or in my logged-in browser and tell me the result, even if I walk away.

Make sure this actually happened: after you perform an action on my Mac or in a logged-in browser, independently verify the real-world postcondition and keep working until it is true or tell me exactly what prevented it.

“Do the approved plan even if I leave the conversation: carry it out across my Mac and logged-in browser, but only while the facts it depends on are still true; stop safely on any mismatch and tell me exactly what happened.”
Handle this private webpage for me: gather the details, prepare the reversible changes, and finish only after I approve the exact result.

When I say ‘send this to Alex’ or ‘book it with Sam,’ resolve the right person across my Mac contacts, calendar, mail, and logged-in sites, tell me the candidates and why, and let me choose by pressing the pendant button before you prepare the action.

Do this across my Mac and logged-in browser, and only tell me it worked when an independent check proves the intended change actually happened; if anything is unreachable or only partly done, say exactly what remains.

Start this on the pendant, let my Mac and private browser carry it out while I move around, and bring the exact unfinished step back to me when I reconnect—without restarting anything or guessing what already happened.
“Finish this across my browser and Mac, even if I leave: use the logged-in page, save the result in my workspace, and tell me only when each step is proven complete.”

“Before you send, buy, delete, or submit anything, give me a compact receipt on the pendant and let me approve it there only if my Mac shows the same receipt; then carry out exactly that approved change and tell me what the other device proves afterward.”

“Put me back exactly where I left off, and let me continue from the pendant.” The system should preserve a live handoff capsule: what I was trying to do, the relevant Mac app/document, authenticated browser tabs and page locations, selected text or draft state, and the next safe action. If the link drops, I can press the pendant button later and hear a concise resume brief; the Mac and browser restore only the reversible context, then wait for my confirmation before changing anything.
Prepare this action across my browser and Mac, show me exactly what will happen, and when I say “approve” execute it once—or tell me precisely why it was blocked.
“Resume the thing that got interrupted.”
“Stop everything now.”

Do this and only tell me it's done once you have independently verified the result—for example, that the file contains the requested text, the reminder exists, or the browser change is visible after reload. If it failed or is only queued, tell me that instead.

Before you send or submit something important, show me the exact final payload on the pendant, let me approve that specific version with one button, then send it from the account that owns the session and bring back proof of what was submitted and where it went.
If I say something while the pendant is offline, carry it out safely when it reconnects—once, with the right current context—and tell me exactly what happened or ask me to resolve a conflict.
Put everything back the way it was before that task, across my Mac and logged-in browser, and show me what was restored and what could not be safely reversed.

“If this condition happens, carry out the bounded plan I gave you and tell me exactly what changed.” For example: if my authenticated travel page reports a cancellation, find an option under my stated limits, prepare it, and only commit automatically if every constraint and freshness check still passes; otherwise wake me on the pendant with the exact decision needed.

“Start this, and keep control of it even if I walk away.” Give me one action baton that can move between the pendant, relay, Mac, and browser: begin a reversible task, show/announce who currently owns it, let me pause or cancel from the pendant, and return a durable proof of exactly what happened—even across a dropped connection.

“That partly failed—repair it without repeating anything that already happened.” After a Mac, browser, or relay action is interrupted, inspect the real state across the relevant surfaces, identify the exact boundary reached, and safely complete or roll back only the missing reversible work. Return a proof of the repaired final state, not merely a retry log.

“Tell me the private part only when it is safe.” Route sensitive results and confirmations to the owner’s pendant only when the paired device proves it is present; otherwise leave a redacted notification on the Mac/dashboard and wait. This should cover logged-in browser findings, account alerts, and action receipts without exposing their contents to nearby people or an unattended speaker.
“Prepare this action on my Mac, but don’t release it until I give the pendant a deliberate physical confirmation—even if the voice link is gone; then tell me exactly what was released.”

When I say “send it” on the pendant, prepare the message on my Mac or logged-in browser, show me the exact recipient and content, wait for a deliberate physical button confirmation, execute once, then verify and report what actually happened.

If an online action is interrupted halfway—such as a booking, purchase, form submission, or account change—tell me whether it actually happened, reconcile the browser, Mac, relay, and pendant state, and give me one safe recovery action instead of making me start over or risk a duplicate.
“Do this everywhere it needs to happen, and tell me one honest result: completed, waiting for me, or unable — with proof of what changed.”
“Pause this private browser task and let me resume it from the pendant when I’m away from my Mac.”

“Do this across my Mac and logged-in browser, but don’t leave me half-done: check everything first, make the reversible changes, ask once before the final commit, and recover cleanly if one side fails.”
“Make my contact details consistent everywhere I use them.”

When I tell you to change something across my Mac and a logged-in website, carry it through as one transaction: show me what changed, recover safely from a dropped connection or partial step, and tell me exactly what still needs my hands.

Let me approve a prepared Mac or logged-in-browser action with one physical press on the pendant, but only when the pendant is demonstrably near my Mac; show me the exact action on the pendant first, and keep it paused if the pendant, relay, or browser session is not the same one that prepared it.
“I’m holding the pendant—commit the prepared transaction now, but only if I press its button within the next 10 seconds.”
“I plugged in the pendant—run a safe end-to-end health check and tell me whether the microphone, 24 kHz playback path, ESP32 bridge, and headphones each work.”
“If the Mac finishes an action while my pendant is disconnected, save the result and tell me exactly once when I reconnect—without rerunning anything.”
“When I’m in the middle of something, protect my attention: pause background work, suppress non-urgent alerts, and bring back only the one item that truly needs me when I’m free.”
“Handle this until you hit a decision only I can make; ask me that one question on the pendant, then continue from the exact step without starting over.”

Do this for me, safely: carry out my spoken goal across my Mac and logged-in browser, and use a physical button press on the pendant as the final confirmation whenever the action would send, submit, delete, or buy. Then tell me exactly what happened.
Save what I am looking at for later.
Undo the last thing you did, but only if it is still safe.
entries.note: Delivered by POST /jobs/undo-last (local-agent/undo.js + jobTracker.js, undo is exercised in jobTracker.test.js): it picks the newest run that can be undone itself and reverses it in reverse order - restore the snapshot, move the file back, delete the copy, put volume and brightness back. The "only if it is still safe" half is real and enforced: shell, keyboard, email and browser steps are declared irreversible and are refused rather than faked, and GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts reports per action whether an undo is possible before anything is attempted. Both routes are live in GET /capabilities.

entries.summary: Lock my private Mac and browser when I walk away, and unlock them only when my pendant is back with me and I tap its button.
Read whatever is currently in front of me on the Mac, one short piece at a time, and let me skip or revisit pieces with the pendant button.
If my pendant is lost or stolen, revoke it immediately, stop it receiving queued audio or commands, and tell me the last trustworthy place and time it was seen.

“I’m leaving.” Lock down my Mac and private browser session: save anything unsaved that can be safely saved, close or hide sensitive windows, pause notifications and media, and tell me exactly what was changed through the pendant; leave a receipt I can undo when I return.

“Hold my focus for the next hour.” Put the Mac in a quiet, visible focus mode, mute or defer nonessential notifications and browser distractions, keep an emergency path available from the pendant’s single button, then restore the exact prior state and report what was restored.

“Mark this for later.” Press the pendant button once while I’m at the Mac to capture the frontmost app, selected text or clipboard, active Safari tab, and timestamp into a private action packet; later I can say “continue the thing I marked” and the system reconstructs the context without me explaining it again.

“I need help.” Or press the pendant’s emergency gesture. Alert my configured contact with my last known location/status and a short, owner-approved message, keep retrying over the Mac/relay path until delivery is verified, and cancel only when I explicitly cancel from the pendant or dashboard.

“Run presentation mode.” While I present, let the pendant’s button advance or go back through Keynote/PowerPoint/browser slides, let me ask the mind to jump to a named slide or display speaker notes on the Mac, and give a clear LED/audio acknowledgement for every transition.

“Fill this out without exposing my private data.” Have the Mac and authenticated browser inspect the form, fetch only the minimum matching values from local sources, fill reversible fields locally, and show me a field-by-field provenance and redaction report before anything leaves the Mac or is submitted.

“Protect me if the pendant disappears.” If the worn device is unexpectedly disconnected or its heartbeat stops, lock the Mac, pause private browser work, revoke only the sessions I have configured as high-risk, and notify me through another channel; distinguish a planned USB unplug from a loss and let me recover safely when the pendant returns.
“If I say ‘do this when the condition is true,’ watch the relevant private page or calendar, and execute the prepared action exactly once when the condition arrives—otherwise leave it untouched.”
“Emergency privacy.” (One press on the pendant should immediately protect my Mac and browser, then tell me what it did.)
“Pause this and let me pick it up later.”
“Let it handle this one task in my account, but give it no more access than this task needs—and revoke it when it’s done.”

When I'm at my Mac and say “make this happen,” use the pendant's physical presence as the authorization: prepare the browser/Mac changes, show me a compact before/after summary, and execute only while I hold the pendant button; releasing it or unplugging the pendant aborts any not-yet-committed step.

Give me a 'walk-away handoff': when I tap the pendant before leaving, freeze the current browser/Mac task into a resumable handoff with the exact tabs, selected text, files, pending jobs, and next safe step; when I tap again later, brief me through the pendant and resume only the steps I approve.

If I hold the pendant's emergency gesture, start a timed safety check: alert me locally, notify my chosen contact with my last confirmed location/status, and escalate only if I do not cancel. Let me cancel from the pendant even if the Mac or voice session is unavailable.

Move an active private browser task between my Mac and another trusted device without copying passwords: package the exact task state and a short-lived capability, let me approve the transfer with the pendant, and reopen it on the destination with secrets remaining in the destination's authenticated browser.

When I press the pendant button, save what I’m looking at as a thought: capture the active Mac app and open browser tab context, classify it as a note, reminder, or idea, and give me a one-sentence spoken acknowledgment. Never send or delete anything.

Put me back in the middle of my last unfinished task. Reopen the exact files and private browser tabs involved, summarize the last successful and failed steps, and ask me for only the next decision you cannot make.
If I walk away while you are carrying out a reversible task, pause cleanly; when I reconnect the pendant, tell me what completed, what is still pending, and offer to continue from the next safe step.

Teach the system a task by doing it once while I narrate. Record the Mac and private-browser steps, identify which values are parameters, and turn it into a reusable routine that I can invoke later from the pendant without repeating the walkthrough.

Before I leave for an appointment, make me a private departure packet: verify the route and timing, gather the relevant meeting files and logged-in page details, put everything in one local folder, and give me a short spoken checklist. Do not contact anyone or change calendar events.

Package everything I need to hand a project to another person: collect the relevant local files, notes, calendar commitments, and logged-in browser facts, remove secrets and personal data, and create a reviewable local handoff folder with a checklist. Do not share it or send it.

“Even with no LTE registration, let me use the pendant today: press the button, speak through the USB-connected pendant/ESP32, and hear the response, with the Mac relaying it to the same conversation.”

“When a Mac or browser job fails, don’t just tell me it failed: inspect the receipt, logs, browser heartbeat, and current Mac state, repair transient problems, retry safely, and tell me exactly what was fixed or why you stopped.”

“Do the private parts on my Mac, but still coordinate everything for me: use my logged-in browser and local files without sending their contents to the relay, then give me a concise answer or execute the approved next step.”
“Repeat the last thing I had you do, but adapt it to what is on screen now, and show me the exact differences before you run it.”
“Tell me whether the pendant is truly usable right now—not merely connected—and, if it isn’t, run a safe loopback test and explain the failing part.”
“Put this page, quote, or result from my private browser onto my phone as a secure handoff, and let me pick it up later on the pendant without making me copy or expose the whole page.”
“I’ve approved this on my pendant—carry out the prepared action now, but only if the physical confirmation is fresh.”
“If that computer task partially succeeded, find out what actually changed, finish only the missing parts, and tell me exactly what you repaired.”
“Walk me through this checklist one step at a time; do the safe computer steps, pause for my pendant confirmation at the risky steps, and let me cancel without touching the Mac.”
“Move this appointment to the best available time, but don’t cancel the current one unless the replacement is confirmed.”
“When I leave my desk, keep the task alive and tell me on the pendant only when I need to make a decision that cannot wait.”
“Give me a private, spoken handoff when I arrive home: what changed while I was away, what decisions are waiting, and what I can safely approve now.”

“Use the details in my logged-in accounts to complete this booking or purchase, but require me to press the pendant’s physical button immediately before the final Submit—and then tell me exactly what was sent.”

“While the pendant is USB-tethered to my Mac, let its button and tiny status light control my current action: press once to capture a thought, press twice to mark it urgent, and hold to cancel the last unsent capture—then read the result back to me.”
“Save the useful thing I’m looking at in Safari to this project.”
“Close out my last meeting.”
“Make a safe-to-share version of this private page and put it in my project.”

When I press the pendant button while looking at something, save a complete 'context card' of what I was doing—active Mac app/document, current browser tab and selected text if available, timestamp, and my short dictated label later—and leave it as a searchable follow-up.

When the pendant disconnects from my Mac or I press its 'leaving' gesture, package the work I was doing into a departure handoff: save open project state and URLs, create a prioritized resume checklist, and read me the first item when I reconnect.

Let me use the pendant's button and audio bridge to work through a spoken queue of pending briefings and receipts: next, repeat, mark heard, and open the referenced item on the Mac, without touching the keyboard.

Move an active conversation and its unfinished plan between my pendant, Mac, and browser without starting over: say 'continue on my Mac' or press the handoff control, and resume with the transcript, evidence, pending approvals, and exactly the next safe step.

Put the whole hive into a physical 'do not act' mode with one deliberate pendant gesture: stop speech and outbound actions, cancel or pause queued work where safe, and hold only a small urgent queue until I explicitly release it.

Tell the hive 'erase the last hour' and have it actually remove the selected conversation's audio, transcripts, browser extracts, Mac snapshots, generated speech, and job-context links across every store, then return a verifiable deletion receipt.
“Only interrupt me when it is genuinely urgent; let me acknowledge it from the pendant.”
“Pin what I’m looking at right now so I can ask about it later.”
“Tell me what is waiting for my review, in order, and let me dismiss or reopen one from the pendant.”
“Put the whole hive in private mode now, and tell me when no pending capture or upload still contains private data.”
“Before you use a logged-in account, prove to me which account and identity you are about to act as.”
“When I say I’m leaving, package exactly where I was across the Mac and browser so I can continue from the pendant or another device.”
“During a meeting, when I tap the pendant, mark that moment and remember what was being discussed; afterward, give me a sourced action list and draft follow-ups.”
“I’m leaving my desk—make sure the document or page I was working on is ready to continue later, and tell me on the pendant exactly where I left off.”
“When I double-tap the pendant, let me speak a quick thought while I’m away from the Mac; turn it into the right note, task, or reminder and read back what you captured.”
“Before you send, buy, publish, delete, or change anything important, ask me to press the pendant; only that physical press should authorize this exact operation.”
“If I set a check-in deadline and then become unreachable, try the pendant, my Mac, and my approved contact channels in order; only escalate after showing that each attempt failed.”
“I’m stepping away—lock everything down.”
“Bookmark exactly where I am; I’ll continue later.”
“The action failed—figure out what went wrong and get me to a safe retry.”
“Move the information from this logged-in page into my local project, but do not send the page contents through the relay.”
“Keep my plan true, not merely recorded.”
“Tell me when the thing I started has actually reached the outside world.”

“Run the wearable audio test.” The Mac should exercise the USB-connected pendant and ESP32 bridge with a known 24 kHz fixture, collect synchronized UART and relay timestamps, verify that audio reaches the headphones, and tell me the measured latency, underruns, and pass/fail result without flashing anything.

“If the wearable test fails, make me a complete repair packet.” Collect the pendant UART, ESP32 serial, relay event trail, and the Mac action receipt, identify the first failing boundary, attach a minimal reproduction command, and leave a redacted incident bundle ready for the engineer—without modifying hardware.

“Can you hear the pendant?” Start a synchronized three-point check: the pendant emits a locally generated chirp, the ESP32 bridge confirms it entered the Bluetooth stream, and the relay/Mac confirm the command round trip. Tell me which exact boundary is audible or broken, with no cloud audio recording and no firmware update.

“Which physical device is mine right now?” Have the pendant, ESP32 bridge, Mac, and relay perform a mutual identity challenge: blink a distinctive LED pattern, play a short bridge tone, return signed device IDs over USB, and show one verified hardware chain before any device-specific action is allowed.

“I’m wearing the pendant—take care of the thing I’m looking at.” Have the system capture the active Safari tab, identify the reversible next step, prepare it on the Mac, and return a one-sentence spoken receipt plus a physical ready/failed signal on the pendant; never submit an irreversible action without my explicit confirmation.

“If that action fails, recover it.” When a browser or Mac action hits a timeout, changed page, or lost connection, have the system diagnose the failure, choose a safe alternate hand (browser bridge, AppleScript/API, or deferred Mac job), retry only idempotent steps, and leave me a concise pendant receipt saying what was recovered and what still needs me.

“Arm this only while I’m holding the pendant.” Let the Mac and browser prepare a high-impact action, but require a device-bound physical gesture on the pendant—such as a long press followed by a second press within 10 seconds—to release the final commit token. Show the target and change in the spoken prompt before arming, and give a local LED result afterward.

“Save this moment so I can resume it later.” From the pendant, capture the active browser tab, the relevant page excerpt, the current Mac application/project, and the last action receipt into one private task capsule.
