Tell me, before I leave, whether I have created an unresolved real-world commitment today—an unanswered message, missed promised follow-up, unpaid item, or appointment risk—and let me resolve it from the pendant with one deliberate, auditable action.

“Use the pendant wheel to choose where this goes, then say ‘send it’.” Let me select Mac Notes, Messages, browser tab, or iPhone from a tactile wheel menu, preview the destination, and physically confirm before the chosen surface receives the captured voice/text item.
“When I say ‘finish this later’, wait for one specific verified condition—such as this browser tab reaching a target state—then perform the next step once and tell me exactly what happened.”

“Use my work account for this, and never fall back to another account.” The system should identify the intended identity, bind execution to the matching logged-in browser session or Mac app, and refuse when the session/account cannot be proven.

“Make this change everywhere I have it open, but show me any place that could not be changed.” The system should find the same logical item across my browser, Mac files, Notes, and mirrored iPhone, apply a staged edit, and return a complete per-surface result instead of silently succeeding on only one copy.
“I asked you to do something, but the computer or network may have timed out. Tell me whether it happened, and recover without sending it twice.”
“Before an important conversation, quietly check that the pendant can deliver speech clearly, and warn me if the audio path is degraded.”
“After you finish, tell me exactly what changed on my Mac or in the browser—not just that the action succeeded.”
“Use my logged-in account to complete this form, but do not show my passwords, payment numbers, private messages, or one-time codes to the AI or relay.”
“When I’m moving, never send or publish anything; queue it and ask me when I’m still.”
“Before you click buy/send/book, re-check the exact price, recipient, and account; if anything changed, stop and tell me what changed.”
“Keep an eye on this page for me and interrupt me only if the status, price, deadline, or required action changes.”
“Make this a private moment.”

When I say “get me into my next meeting,” have the system find the next calendar event, open the right meeting URL in the authenticated browser, verify that the page is actually ready, and tell me on the pendant whether I’m in or what blocked it.

After I ask you to do something important, give me a truthful ‘finished / blocked / needs me’ result on the pendant, and keep trying only the safe recovery steps when the Mac or browser drops offline.

When I bookmark a moment on the pendant, turn it into a useful follow-up automatically: capture what I was looking at, create a cited note, and—if I say ‘remind me’—schedule the reminder with the source attached.

When I ask you to fill out a form with my usual details, identify the fields, fetch the matching values privately from my Mac, show me only the categories and destination on the pendant, and release the actual values only after I approve that exact field set.

If I take the pendant off or it detects an unusual motion pattern, immediately freeze staged computer actions and sensitive browser sessions, then tell me what was stopped when I put it back on or explicitly recover it.

Let me say “make this safe to share” while viewing a document or webpage, and have the system produce a redacted copy, show me exactly what categories were removed on the pendant, and place the result beside the original without overwriting it.
“What are the four newest things on my Safari Reading List, and open the one I mean when I say ‘the second one’?”
“While I’m listening to the daily research brief, press the pendant’s bookmark button when I hear something important, and later give me the exact source and timestamp for each mark.”
“I’m about to leave my desk. Save the current browser page, my draft, and a spoken handoff so I can continue from the pendant later—without sending anything.”
“Private mode. Let my Mac receive what I say, but do not send the audio or transcript to the relay or model.”
“Emergency revoke.” Cancel every pending action, invalidate every approval, and erase unsent drafts and queued browser commands everywhere, then tell me what was actually revoked.
“Tell me exactly what crossed the privacy boundary for this task: which device saw my words, which app saw the result, what was retained, and when it expires.”
When I say “pause this and bring it back later,” save exactly where I am across the pendant, Mac, and browser, then restore that work later without guessing.
Before you do a delayed or multi-step task for me, tell me whether the Mac and browser are still the same ones I authorized; if not, pause and ask me instead of acting on stale state.

When I say “send this to my phone when it’s ready,” prepare the result on my Mac or browser, hand it to my real iPhone through iPhone Mirroring, and tell me whether it was actually delivered—not merely queued.

When I say “keep a record of this purchase,” capture a tamper-evident private evidence bundle from the logged-in browser and Mac—receipt, relevant URL, timestamp, and my short voice annotation—and let me retrieve or export it later.

For the next two hours, watch this logged-in page or Mac condition and alert me on the pendant only when it changes in the way I described; show me the evidence and stop watching automatically at the deadline.

“Make this multi-step change across my Mac and browser, but before anything irreversible, tell me exactly what will change; only continue if I approve the concrete diff, and prove afterward that every step landed.”

“At the time I specified, check that the real-world preconditions are still true, then do the action across my Mac/browser; if anything changed, don't guess—tell me on the pendant and leave a resumable approval waiting.”

“If something I asked you to do partially failed or became unverifiable, stop all retries, gather the minimum fresh evidence, and give me one safe recovery choice on the pendant—resume, undo what definitely happened, or abandon.”
“When I’m on a phone call, keep a private running record of decisions and commitments, and afterward turn only the confirmed action items into reminders or calendar drafts.”
“Before I share this file or paste this text anywhere, find sensitive details, show me exactly what would leave my devices, and let me approve a redacted version or cancel.”

“Create the final document from these sources, keep a private provenance map of what came from where, and when a source changes later, tell me exactly which claims or sections are now stale instead of silently rewriting it.”
"When I press the bookmark button, save what I was looking at—not just the time—and make it useful later."
"Before we start talking, tell me if the pendant audio path is actually healthy, and degrade safely if it isn't."
"After you do it, show me exactly what was touched and what you deliberately did not read—without exposing the private contents."
If my Mac restarts or the browser disconnects halfway through something I asked you to do, resume it safely without doing it twice.
When something may have happened but you cannot prove it, tell me exactly what is unknown and give me the safest next step instead of retrying blindly.
Show me which pending action needs my attention, let me scroll through them on the pendant, and let me approve or cancel exactly one without opening my phone.

Before sending, buying, deleting, or changing anything, warn me if the Mac or browser is in the wrong account or workspace, and let me switch to the right one without exposing its contents to the pendant.
Undo the last thing you did, but only if you can prove the reversal will not damage anything else; otherwise show me the safest manual recovery.
Why did that happen? Show me a human-readable chain from my spoken request to the exact Mac/browser changes, approvals, and evidence, including where uncertainty entered.
“Keep track of the promises I make, even casually. If I say I’ll send something, call someone, or follow up, remind me at the right time and prepare whatever I need.”
“I’m with other people now—keep helping, but don’t reveal anything private or use my logged-in accounts unless I explicitly ask.”
“Start this, and if I get interrupted or lose connection, keep my place and pick it back up when I’m ready.”
“When I’m in a meeting or focused, protect my attention; let only truly urgent things through, and catch me up afterward.”
“Remember the commitments I make in conversation, and help me keep them without making promises on my behalf.”
“Save this thought for the next time I’m looking at this project, and bring it back without interrupting me.”
“Keep track of the promises I make, and tell me only when one is at risk of being missed.”
“Keep track of the promises and deadlines I make, and only remind me when one is at risk.”
“I’m going offline for a while—prepare what I need, and catch me up on only what changed when I’m back.”
“Before I walk into this conversation, give me the context I need—and afterward, turn what I explicitly marked into a follow-up plan without sending anything.”

“I can’t deal with this now—bring it back to me later.” Then, at the right time, remind me with the exact page, message, or file I was looking at and a one-sentence explanation of what I meant to do; let me snooze or finish it by voice.
“Protect my attention. While I’m working or in a meeting, decide which incoming things truly deserve an interruption; quietly queue the rest, and tell me afterward what you held back and why.”
“Only interrupt me when something truly matters; otherwise keep a quiet queue and tell me at the right time.”
“While I’m away, carry this through within the limits I set—and stop, ask, or hand it back whenever the situation exceeds those limits.”
“I’m back—catch me up on anything you did or anything that changed while I was away, and tell me the one thing I should do next.”
entries.note: Duplicate of cap-4aab3adb (implemented). GET /catchup covers both what the agent did and what changed; GET /catchup/needs-me ranks what is left.

entries.summary: “Before I commit to this, show me what it will make harder, what it displaces, and the safest alternative.”
“I’m back—what happened while I was away?”
entries.note: Duplicate of cap-4aab3adb (implemented).

entries.summary: “Put us in silent mode—I need to use you without speaking or taking out my phone.”
“Don’t interrupt me unless it’s important; if I’m busy, queue it and tell me at the right moment.”
“If I walk away, pause anything that could change the world, and only resume it when I’m back and the context is still valid.”
“Only interrupt me when it is genuinely worth breaking my concentration; otherwise queue it and catch me at the next natural pause.”
“When I double-press the pendant, make the whole system private until I say otherwise.”
When I make a consequential decision out loud, capture what I decided, the evidence and assumptions behind it, and—if I name a date—check back later and tell me whether reality matched the bet.
Keep this private: do the work, but don't say the answer out loud—show it on my Mac and give me only a discreet pendant signal when it's ready.
Before I commit to this, show me the likely consequences of each option using my actual calendar, messages, files, and logged-in services—and tell me what assumption would change your recommendation.
“If that failed because something is disconnected, fix the connection if you can, then try again; otherwise leave me a one-sentence explanation and a ready-to-resume action.”
“Keep an eye on whether today’s plan is still realistic. If a meeting, unfinished task, or new deadline makes it impossible, tell me what changed and give me the smallest useful replanning choice.”
“Handle this privately.”
“Do this wherever you can, and if something is blocked, tell me exactly what I need to reconnect.”
“Stop everything you’re doing for me right now.”
“Without asking, make it obvious whether you heard me, are working, are blocked, or are finished—and tell me what you need if blocked.”
“Only interrupt me when it truly matters; otherwise collect it and bring it to me at the next good moment.”
“When I make an important decision, remember what I decided, why, what evidence I used, and when I should revisit it—then let me ask you about it months later.”
While I listen to my brief on the pendant, let me say “why?” or “open that,” and have you explain the evidence or open the exact source on my Mac without losing my place.
When I hear something in a brief, let me say “save that,” “remind me Friday,” or “add this to the email draft,” and have it capture the exact item and source, then resume where I was.

When I ask something sensitive while I’m around other people, answer privately through the safest available surface—haptic confirmation on the pendant and a discreet Mac or phone display—instead of speaking the secret aloud, and let me switch back when I’m alone.
“If this takes a while, keep going—but stop and ask me if the facts or my intention changed before you do anything consequential.”
“When your sources disagree, don't guess—tell me the conflict in one sentence, let me choose which source to trust, and remember that choice for this situation.”
“I have to go—keep this moving, and when I’m back tell me only what changed and what you still need from me.”
“Warn me before my commitments collide, and give me the smallest fix I can approve.”
“If something you planned is no longer true, don’t do it—recheck the important details and ask me only when the change matters.”
“Keep working on this, but if the facts change before you act, stop and tell me exactly what changed; never finish a stale plan.”

When I mention something I might want to do, keep it as a tentative decision, quietly gather the missing context, and later ask me one precise question before preparing the next step—without making me repeat myself.
Before I commit to this, show me what it will change across my calendar, inbox, files, browser tasks, and pending promises—and let me compare two options without changing anything.
“Help me decide this.” Then give me the best option, what could change the answer, and let me choose it from the pendant without reopening all the tabs.

“That’s wrong—fix it everywhere.” Then show me what future briefs, plans, reminders, and pending browser/Mac actions relied on the wrong fact, let me choose the replacements, and prevent the stale version from resurfacing.
“Do this, and if my Mac or browser isn’t ready, don’t pretend—pause it, tell me what’s blocked, and resume automatically when it’s safe.”
“Before you make a plan from my accounts, tell me when my information conflicts, ask me the one question that would resolve it, and keep the plan safely provisional until I answer.”
Before I say yes to this, tell me what it will cause elsewhere in my life—and show me the safest alternatives.
“I have 15 minutes—what should I do right now?” (or “I’m overloaded; what can wait?”)

“Protect my attention: notice what becomes urgent across my logged-in tabs, calendar, and Mac, hold non-urgent things, and tell me at the next safe moment—briefly on the pendant, with the evidence waiting on my Mac.”
“When my commitments collide, tell me which promise is actually at risk and prepare the least-cost way to resolve it.”

“Keep me from missing the things I implicitly promised: find deadlines and commitments across my logged-in mail, calendar, work pages, and local notes, tell me what matters next, and quietly prepare the reversible parts before the deadline.”
“When a new request would overload me or conflict with something I already committed to, tell me plainly, show me the tradeoff, and prepare a kind reply or rescheduling option I can approve.”
“Don’t let me drop the promises I make.”
“Before I commit to this, tell me what it will collide with—and help me make room if I still want it.”
“Take care of this, even if I leave or one of my devices goes offline—when I come back, show me exactly what is finished, what changed underneath us, and the one decision I still need to make.”

“While I’m unavailable, protect my time: triage incoming requests, identify what conflicts with my real commitments, and negotiate a reasonable alternative only within rules I’ve approved. Tell me what you accepted, declined, or left for me.”
“Only interrupt me when it is genuinely worth breaking my concentration—and if I miss it, keep escalating until the right moment.”
“When my calendar, email, and web accounts disagree, don't guess—tell me what conflicts, ask the one question that resolves it, and make the correction everywhere it belongs.”
“Use my private accounts to get things done, but keep my passwords and unrelated personal data out of the AI—and show me exactly what each part was allowed to see.”
Before I commit to this, check what I'm overlooking and give me the safest next step.
If I say yes to this, what will it cost me—and what would have to move?

“What am I on the hook for, and what should I decide next?” Give me one short, sourced list of commitments across my calendar, mail, notes, and logged-in work pages; merge duplicates, flag contradictory or stale evidence, rank by deadline and consequence, recommend the next reversible step, and let me approve any follow-up draft without sending it.

“If I say yes to this, what does it displace, and can I realistically keep the promise?” Given a message, invitation, or request I am viewing, show me the hidden schedule, travel, workload, and dependency consequences; offer three honest responses (accept, decline, or propose a bounded alternative) and draft the chosen reply for my approval without sending it.
“Why are you suggesting this, and what exactly will happen if I say yes?” (Also: “Stop using that source for this.”)
“Tell me what actually matters today, and only interrupt me when the evidence changes or two of my sources disagree.”
“Before I commit to this, show me what each option would do to my actual schedule, messages, files, and accounts—and let me choose without changing anything yet.”
Let me give the pendant temporary permission to handle this one kind of task, and have it expire automatically when the task is done or after I say how long.

When I double-press the pendant, put the whole hive in privacy mode until I release it: stop sending or reading sensitive context, pause Mac/browser observation, and tell me when it is safe to resume.

Let me say “rehearse this” and have the pendant, Mac, browser, and relay work out the whole task without changing anything, then tell me exactly what would happen, what information would leave my devices, and where you would stop for approval.
“Decide what deserves my attention now. Give me one short spoken brief when I have a spare moment, defer the rest, and let me say ‘why?’ or ‘do it’ to continue from the exact item.”

“Catch conflicts in my real life before they become mistakes—like two commitments at once, a deadline that depends on an unavailable document, or a travel plan that no longer fits—and give me the smallest decision I need to make.”
“If I’m about to miss something important, rescue it for me: figure out what is actually due, prepare the smallest useful next step, and ask me only when my approval is needed.”
“Before I agree to anything new, tell me what it will displace, whether I actually have room for it, and prepare the kindest way to say no or renegotiate if I don’t.”
“Before I approve this, tell me whether anything important changed since you prepared it.”
“Make this conversation safe to continue with other people around.”

“Keep me from dropping the people I care about: notice when a meaningful conversation or promise needs follow-up, show me the evidence, and prepare a personal draft or reminder—never send anything unless I approve.”

“When something changes my day, repair the rest of it: notice cancellations, delays, or new commitments across my calendar, mail, and logged-in services; show me what conflicts, suggest the smallest workable reshuffle, and prepare the reminders or drafts needed to recover.”

Before you act, tell me whether you can actually reach the right device and whether the time zone is settled; if not, ask me one short question and wait. Never say something happened when it only looked like it did.
When I travel or my devices disagree about time, ask whether I mean home time or where I am before creating anything, and remember that choice only for this task.

If I’m in public or someone else may hear me, give me the useful answer without exposing private details: speak a safe summary on the pendant and put the exact names, amounts, links, or account content on my private Mac/browser screen. Let me say 'private' or 'say it all' to change the mode for this task.
“Keep track of the promises I make, and help me close the loop.”
“When something changes my day, re-plan the rest of it and tell me the one next thing to do.”
“If you can do this within these limits, just handle it; otherwise ask me.” For example: “Rebook my flight to arrive before six, under $300, and use the same airline if possible.”

“Before I commit to this, show me what saying yes will cost.” For an invitation, appointment, purchase, or deadline, compare the real alternatives and tell me the likely schedule, travel, money, preparation, and privacy consequences—without changing anything.
“Queue anything that needs my approval, and let me safely approve it from the pendant when I have a moment.”
“I’m around people—keep helping, but don’t reveal anything aloud or on a screen someone can see.”
“If something I asked you to do finishes—or gets stuck—while I’m away, tell me what actually happened and give me the one next thing I can do.”
“When I leave somewhere, check the things I care about and tell me only what is definitely handled—and what I need to fix.”
“Take care of this end to end, and don't tell me it's done until you can verify the outcome.”
“Build me an evidence packet for this dispute or appeal, but do not submit anything.”
“Keep me from missing the one thing that matters today, but don’t interrupt me for everything.”
“Something went wrong with this account or purchase—build me the strongest case without sending anything.”
“Learn how much freedom I want: handle routine, reversible things without bothering me, but ask at the right boundary—and show me when you think my boundary should change.”
“Let me approve a plan once with conditions—if the price, wording, recipient, and deadline stay within these limits, finish it; otherwise pause and ask me.”
“I have too many competing commitments—tell me what to do first, what to defer, and prepare the messages or reschedules, but don’t send anything without me.”
“When I’m in a meeting, driving, or clearly overloaded, protect my attention: let only truly urgent things through, keep the rest moving, and show me what you deferred afterward.”
“Before I say yes to a new commitment, tell me whether I can realistically keep it, what it will displace, and give me a smaller promise I can safely make instead.”
“When you tell me something is done, make sure it really happened; if a device is offline or permission is missing, tell me plainly and keep the task resumable.”
“Fix the connection so you can act on my Mac again, and tell me exactly what I need to approve.”
“If I say yes to this, what else does it affect—and what is the least disruptive alternative?”
“Before you use another device or service, show me the smallest amount of my information you need to share, and let me approve or redact it.”
“What should I do next?” — and, if I have enough time, prepare the best next step for me.
“Privacy mode.” Make sure nothing is listening, recording, or reading my private screens until I turn it back on.
“If the connection or my Mac disappears halfway through, pick up exactly where we left off—without repeating an action or losing what I said.”
“If something seems wrong and I stop responding, check on me in stages and get help without exposing my private data.”
“Only interrupt me when it is worth interrupting me; otherwise queue it and give me one coherent update later.”
“If I haven’t dealt with this by Friday, make sure the right person knows—but don’t send anything unless the conditions are actually met.”
“Did that actually get done?” — after I ask the system to do something, give me a short answer about the real-world result, not merely whether a command was dispatched.
“If this isn’t done by Friday at 3, remind me and prepare the next step.”
“Notice when I keep getting stuck on the same kind of thing, and suggest one small change that would make it easier next time.”
“Do this, and tell me only when you can prove it worked.”
“Keep the conversation natural, even when the connection is busy or I talk over you.”
Tell me what I can safely ignore today, and keep anything risky from slipping through.
Before I say yes to something, tell me what it will really cost me and give me a reply I can send.

“When my scheduled brief runs, tell me exactly which sources were checked, which were unavailable or stale, and keep retrying the missing parts—never say it completed when it only produced a partial answer.”

“If I double-press and hold the pendant, make the whole AI hive go private immediately: stop talking, cancel queued actions, freeze browser and Mac control, revoke active sessions, and do not send or retain anything else until I explicitly unlock it.”

“What do I actually know about this?” — reconcile the claims in my mail, calendar, notes, and logged-in pages, show what is confirmed versus assumed or contradicted, and keep the answer current until I tell you it is settled.

“Help me practice this difficult conversation.” Use the context I authorize from my notes, calendar, mail, and relevant browser pages to role-play the other person, challenge my assumptions, and leave me with a concise set of points and boundaries I can recall from the pendant.
“Before you submit or send this, tell me if anything private is about to reach the wrong person or a public site, and fix it if I want.”
“Forget everything about this topic everywhere, and prove what was deleted and what could not be reached.”

“Did that actually happen?” After you act through my Mac or a logged-in site, prove the external result—not just that you clicked—and tell me if it is confirmed, probably done, still pending, or unknown.

“Before you change anything, make sure it is the right account and the right person.” Bind every browser or Mac action to the owner’s intended identity and workspace, detect account/profile changes before and during the task, and refuse to proceed when identity evidence conflicts.

“Before you act, tell me what you can actually reach right now, what is stale or offline, and whether the result will be verified. If a surface drops out, keep the request safe and tell me what remains.”

“If I made this an automatic rule, show me what you would have done over the last week, which cases would have needed my approval, and where the rule would have gone wrong—without actually changing anything.”

“Protect my energy this week: look across my calendar, reminders, unfinished work, travel, and recent interruptions; show me where the load is likely to exceed what I can realistically do, then suggest specific swaps or deferrals for my approval.”

“I got interrupted—pick up exactly where I left off.” The pendant should give me a 20-second resume briefing, reopen the relevant Mac document and browser tabs, and offer the single next step without repeating work or sending anything.

“What promises have I made recently that I’m quietly failing to keep?” Give me a private, evidence-linked list of commitments inferred from my conversations, calendar, notes, and logged-in pages; rank the ones whose silence is most likely to hurt someone, and prepare a repair plan without contacting anyone.
“If the pendant’s audio path breaks or changes quality, keep the conversation going without making me repeat myself, and tell me clearly what happened.”

“Put me in a private bubble when I ask: keep sensitive answers and account details off nearby screens and speakers, let me review or act through the pendant, and automatically restore my normal workspace when I leave private mode.”

When I say “pause this and come back later,” save exactly where we are across my pendant, Mac, and browser, then later give me a 20-second spoken recap and let me resume without reconstructing the task.

Make sure my scheduled brief actually reaches me. If the pendant cannot play it, keep a durable copy, retry when the link returns, and tell me exactly what was missed instead of claiming it was delivered.

I’m with other people—switch to discreet mode. From now on, keep private names, message text, account details, and page contents off the speaker and show me only safe summaries or a vibration cue until I turn it off.

I lost my pendant. Lock it and revoke its access everywhere now—stop queued audio, invalidate browser and Mac control, and tell me what was successfully frozen. If it comes back, make me re-pair it before anything resumes.
“Give me one useful update, not five separate briefings—and if I miss it, catch me up without repeating what I already heard.”
entries.note: Duplicate of cap-4aab3adb (implemented). Not repeating what was already heard is what local-agent/catchupClock.js tracks, and the watch equivalent is POST /watches/:watchId/ack.

entries.summary: “When you do something for me, don’t just say it ran—tell me whether the outside world actually reflects the result, and warn me if it didn’t.”
“For anything important, have two independent parts of my system agree it happened—or keep it pending and bring me the disagreement.”
“When I actually leave home, give me a two-minute departure check tailored to where I’m going—only interrupt me for something I can still fix, and keep the rest queued.”

“Stop everything.” (or long-press the pendant button) should immediately silence the pendant, freeze new automation, cancel queued Mac/browser work, and give me a private receipt of what was stopped; “resume” should show the exact next unverified steps before anything continues.

“Private mode” should follow me across the pendant, Mac, and browser: when I tap the pendant or enter a sensitive calendar context, the system should stop speaking private content aloud, prevent private page text from entering model context, pause background jobs that could expose it, and show me a small local indication of the active boundary. When I leave, it should not silently resume disclosure; it should give me a concise review of what was withheld and let me restore normal mode.

“Did that actually happen?” — for any task you carried out, verify it across the relevant surfaces and tell me in one short spoken sentence whether it is verified, contradicted, or still unknown, with the reason and the next safe step.

“Learn what worked.” After I make a consequential choice through the pendant, Mac, or a logged-in browser, check the result later, ask me once whether it worked for me, and use that answer to improve future recommendations—without keeping the private source material.
“Before I head out, make sure this appointment or trip is actually ready.”
“After this trip or project, reconcile what actually happened and leave me only the loose ends.”
“I got interrupted—catch me up from where I left off.”
“Why did I decide this, and what would change my mind?”

When a request involving my private accounts fails, tell me exactly why, give me the shortest repair step on the right device, and retry the original request automatically once access is restored—without repeating work or exposing account contents.

When I say “not now” or get interrupted, remember exactly what I was doing across the pendant, Mac, and browser, wait for a sensible boundary, and offer one short resume prompt—not a generic reminder.

Before you use a private page, document, or message to answer me, show me a one-line privacy preview—what source is being used, what sensitive fields will leave the device, and whether the answer can stay local—then proceed with the safest route.

“Did that actually happen?” Give me a truthful answer across the pendant, relay, Mac, and browser: what was requested, what each surface confirmed, what is still only claimed, and the safest next step if anything failed.

“Stop everything I asked you to do.” A deliberate long press on the pendant must immediately stop speech and issue a single cancellation across every active Mac, browser, relay, and background job—even if the network is down—and later show me exactly what was stopped, what could not be stopped, and whether anything irreversible had already happened.
“If the connection gets bad while I’m talking, don’t lose what I said—keep the conversation coherent and tell me only if you truly need me to repeat something.”
“Let me know silently when something important is ready, and let me approve or dismiss it without speaking or taking out my phone.”

“Before you schedule anything or tell me a time-sensitive deadline, make sure your clocks and time zones agree. If they don’t, tell me the conflict in one sentence and ask which time zone to use; never silently guess.”

“Before you send or submit anything on my behalf, tell me which account and identity it will use, who will receive it, and whether any private information crosses accounts; warn me if the browser tab, Mac app, or saved login is not the identity I intended.”

“Keep my schedules and spoken briefs on the right local time. If my Mac, pendant, or saved preference disagree, warn me before moving anything, and show me which timezone each upcoming item will use.”

“When you have a sensitive action ready—send this email, submit this form, buy this, or delete this—read me a short, exact summary and let me approve it with a physical double-press on the pendant. Bind that approval to exactly what I heard, and refuse if anything changed.”
“What am I waiting on?” Then, whenever an expected reply or task is late, give me one short spoken nudge and prepare (but never send) the follow-up.
“Make a temporary handoff for Alex: give them only what they need to finish this, let them ask questions, and revoke it tomorrow.”
When something I ask fails, tell me what actually blocked it, test the safe alternatives you can reach, and give me the smallest next step to fix it—without making me repeat the request.
Before you call a scheduled brief or background task complete, check what sources it actually reached, tell me what was missing or stale, and offer to rerun only the missing parts.

When I ask “did that actually happen?”, give me a plain-language answer separating attempted, accepted by the local app, completed by the remote service, and independently observed afterward—then tell me what remains uncertain and whether a safe retry exists.

Keep private things private: when I say a secret, personal number, or anything in 'private mode', let me continue using the pendant and my Mac/browser without sending that content to the cloud or putting it in ordinary memory. Later, show me exactly what was withheld and let me explicitly reveal it if needed.

Give me a genuinely private way to use the pendant: when I say 'private', I can dictate a secret or sensitive detail, have it used in one local task on my Mac or in a specific browser tab, and be certain it never entered the cloud transcript, ordinary memory, logs, or receipts.
“Read my private brief, but keep it private if anyone is nearby.”
“Give me my morning brief, but never pretend an account was checked if it wasn’t; use whichever connection works and tell me exactly what is still unknown.”
“When I correct how you handle something, turn that correction into a rule I can review, test on recent examples, and apply everywhere.”
“Look at the commitments I am about to make and warn me when they exceed the time or energy I have, then draft a kind way to decline or renegotiate—without sending anything.”
“What should I do next?” — Give me three realistic choices for the next hour, ranked by what matters most, and if I choose one, set up the reversible pieces for me.
“Before you use another device or service for this, show me what information will leave each surface, what will stay local, and let me approve a redacted version.”

Before I accept or schedule a meeting, tell me how it affects the rest of my day and suggest the least disruptive time, including travel and preparation; never book or move anything without my approval.

I’m overloaded today—make me a graceful degradation plan: tell me what I can safely skip, defer, shorten, or delegate, explain who will be affected and why, draft any needed messages, and let me approve changes one at a time.
“If I promise someone something, remember it, help me do it, and tell me before I let it slip.”

“When I say ‘coach me,’ quietly help me navigate a difficult conversation: remind me of the relevant context, warn me if I am about to make a commitment I cannot keep, and give me one short option for what to say next.”

“Did that actually happen?” — after you do something across my Mac or logged-in browser, prove the resulting state changed, tell me what was verified and where, and flag any mismatch instead of calling it done.
“Before I send this, make sure it is going to the right person and account.”
“Why did I agree to this, and are the reasons I had then still true?”
“That didn’t work—tell me why, fix whatever is safe, and either finish it or tell me the one thing I need to do.”
“Remember why I decided this, and remind me of that reason when the decision comes back up.”
“What did you decide not to tell me, and why?”
“Wrap up that meeting.” Then give me a 60-second debrief: what was decided, who owns what, deadlines, and drafts for any follow-ups—without sending anything.

“Coach me through this conversation.” While I have the pendant armed, listen for ambiguity or a commitment I may regret, and discreetly suggest one short clarifying question or boundary—without speaking to the other person or saving the conversation unless I ask.

“Did that actually reach me?” — For any spoken answer, briefing, or Mac job, show whether it was generated, accepted by the relay, downloaded by my pendant, and played; if any link is missing, say exactly which one and keep retrying safely.

“Take me back to what was true when I made that decision.” Show a dated, evidence-linked snapshot of my relevant calendar, mail, browser pages, Mac files, conversations, and pending tasks, then show only what changed afterward and which assumptions are no longer true.
“When I walk away from my Mac, save exactly where I was and what I meant to do; when I come back or ask from the pendant, give me a 20-second handoff and let me resume without hunting.”
“I’m going into a meeting. For the next hour, watch this thread and handle only routine, reversible follow-ups; tell me if anything important changes, and let me stop it from the pendant.”

“During this conversation, quietly tell me if I’m about to promise something that conflicts with my calendar, existing commitments, or a private account deadline—and save only the commitments I approve.”

“After my meetings, help me close the loop.” When a calendar event ends, ask me (through the pendant) for a quick voice debrief, extract decisions/owners/deadlines, update my private notes and reminders, and prepare—not send—any follow-up messages or browser forms. Show me the evidence and let me correct it before anything external changes.

“Keep my promises feasible.” Continuously detect when my calendar, travel, reminders, private notes, and authenticated work commitments make two obligations impossible or dangerously tight. Ask me on the pendant only when a real conflict is found, explain the evidence and tradeoff, then prepare the smallest set of reschedules, decline messages, or browser changes that would restore feasibility for my approval.
“Don’t tell me something is done until you’ve verified it. If it failed, say what actually happened and what I should do next.”

“When I ask ‘why did I decide this?’ or ‘where did I see that?’, reconstruct the decision or fact from my own recent conversations, Mac documents, calendar, mail, and logged-in browser pages, with the original evidence and what is still uncertain.”
“I’m leaving my desk” — save exactly where I am, tell me what I’m walking away from, and when I return give me a one-sentence restart plan with the right tabs and files ready.
“If I don’t hear back from them by Friday, remind me and draft the right follow-up.”
“Find subscriptions and recurring charges I’m probably not using, show me the evidence, and prepare cancellations—but don’t cancel anything yet.”
“I’m leaving now—what do I need, where am I going, and is there anything I must handle before I go?”
“Before I join this meeting, tell me what information is safe to discuss, what I should keep private, and which open tabs or files I should close.”
“Pause there—I need to deal with this. When I say resume, continue exactly where we left off, and tell me if anything changed while I was away.”
“Give this one action a 10-minute authorization from my pendant, and revoke it automatically if I walk away or the facts change.”

“I’m back—what was I in the middle of, and what should I do next?” Give me one trustworthy resume card assembled from my pendant conversation, Mac work, browser tabs, calendar, and unfinished jobs; let me say continue, park it, or discard it.

“How will this land?” Before I reply to this person, show me the likely interpretations, what I may be implicitly promising, and three short replies in my voice—considering the current thread, our recent calendar context, and whether I have already left them waiting. Do not send anything.
“Make sure my routines run at the right local time, and tell me if anything is off.”
“When something important arrives or needs my approval, let me feel it privately; use different tap patterns for urgent, routine, and waiting-for-me, and let me acknowledge it without speaking.”
Before I commit to this, can I realistically keep the promise?
If I do this, what else will it affect?
Should I say yes to this?

When I ask “what did I miss?”, give me a short, chronological account of important things that happened since I last checked—my pendant conversations, Mac/browser work, scheduled routines, and watched pages—with links, unfinished items, and explicit unknowns.
entries.note: Duplicate of cap-4aab3adb (implemented). The chronological account across pendant conversations, Mac/browser work and routines is local-agent/catchupSources.js; "since I last checked" is local-agent/catchupClock.js.

entries.summary: What changed in my world since [a time or event]? Compare my calendar, messages, important files, browser accounts, and ongoing work against that exact baseline, and tell me only meaningful changes with evidence.
“When I walk into a meeting, get me ready; while I’m there, remember the loose ends; when I leave, turn them into a clean follow-up queue.”

“Let me bring another person into a private AI-assisted conversation safely: make consent and recording state obvious, help us understand each other in real time, and give both of us control over what summary survives.”
“Before I leave for an appointment or trip, make sure I can actually get there.”
“I lost my pendant—lock it down, keep my private work safe, and help me recover without losing my notes.”

“Can I safely walk away from this?” Give me one honest spoken answer about whether the work will finish without me, what could still require my approval, and how you will tell me when it is done. If it is not safe, stop or convert it into a reviewable handoff.

“If I change this, what else will it affect?” Before I approve a consequential change, show me a compact what-if map across my calendar, commitments, travel, private web accounts, files, and pending agent work: what becomes invalid, who may need a message, what deadlines move, and the safest alternative. Do not change anything until I choose.

When something genuinely urgent happens in my mail, calendar, or logged-in browser, alert me silently with a distinct vibration pattern, and let one pendant tap tell me whether it is worth speaking aloud.

Run a seven-day experiment for me: turn a specific intention into tiny check-ins, notice whether it is helping from my explicit replies and completed actions, and give me a verdict with evidence and a recommendation to keep, change, or stop.
“After this conversation, turn the commitments I made into a reviewable action list.”
“Before I share this, make the safest version for that person and tell me what you removed.”
“When I make an important decision, remember what I expected, then later tell me whether reality matched—and what I should learn.”
“Help me run a small, reversible experiment on my life or work, then tell me whether it actually helped.”

When I correct you—like changing a reminder time, shortening a briefing, or rejecting a browser draft—remember that preference and quietly apply it next time, while showing me what you learned and letting me forget it.

Before I say yes to something, let me ask, “What does this commitment cost me?” Have you inspect my calendar, active work, travel, and existing promises, then give me a short consequence forecast with conflicts, hidden preparation, and what I would have to drop—without contacting anyone or changing anything.

“Translate this conversation for me, quietly.” The pendant should listen only while I hold the button, speak a concise translation through my earpiece, and show the original plus translation on my Mac when I want to review it.
“If I say I’ll do something, remember the promise, figure out the next concrete step, and bring it back to me at the right moment—without nagging me.”
“Show me what I knew, what I had promised, and what changed when I made that decision.”
“Before I act on an important detail, tell me if my sources disagree—and show me the smallest thing I can check to resolve it.”
When a meeting starts, quietly get me ready, help me capture commitments during it, and leave me a reviewable follow-up packet afterward.
Before I commit to a time, deadline, or promise anywhere, quietly tell me if it will make another commitment impossible and suggest the safest wording or alternative.
“That’s not what I meant—fix the last thing you did.”
“I lost my pendant. Lock it now, keep my information safe, and let me continue from my Mac without losing my place.”

“Hold this for me until I have a quiet ten minutes.” The pendant should save what I said, have the relay and my Mac/browser gather only the relevant private context, and later give me a short cited audio packet with the decision or next step—without sending, submitting, or changing anything.

“Answer me privately; I’m in public.” The pendant should classify whether the reply contains sensitive information, keep private evidence on the Mac/browser, and deliver the answer through a private listening channel—or silently defer it—rather than speaking it aloud around other people.
“Read me the brief. If I say ‘why?’, show me the source and let me open it on my Mac.”
“When your sources disagree, don’t guess. Tell me what conflicts, ask the one question that resolves it, and remember the answer for next time.”
“Why did we decide that? Reconstruct the short chain of evidence, assumptions, and approvals that led to it, and tell me what has changed since.”
“Forget everything about that topic everywhere.”
“Tell me when my commitments conflict, and give me the least-painful way out.”
“Learn how I like things handled, but ask before you make a new rule.”
“Help me negotiate this without committing me to anything.”
“I’m in the middle of something—hold this thought, work out what’s needed, and bring me back to the exact next decision when I’m free.”
“Before you use my Mac or logged-in browser for this, tell me exactly what private information would leave my devices, remove anything unnecessary, and let me approve the smallest safe version.”

“Keep track of the things I promise people—including things I say casually—and, at the right time, remind me with the context I need; let me mark it done or prepare the follow-up without sending anything.”
“When I leave home, work, or another place I choose, quietly check where I’m going next and tell me what I need to bring, finish, or remember before I get there.”

“Am I ready to leave?” Give me a 20-second departure check from my pendant: next calendar commitment and travel buffer, current weather, battery/connectivity, and any reservation or message that makes leaving urgent. If something is missing, say exactly what—not a generic failure—and never send or change anything.

“Let the pendant quietly tap me when something important is ready—such as a private browser result, a waiting approval, or a time-critical calendar change—and let me press once to hear the short explanation or twice to defer it. I should be able to use this in a meeting or on a noisy street without my phone speaking aloud.”

Keep my pendant useful all day: when its battery or connection is getting weak, quietly move non-urgent work to my Mac or the relay, save anything needed for later, and only interrupt me if I must act before the device goes offline.
If I get interrupted halfway through something, save exactly where we were and let me safely resume it later from the pendant.
When I leave something somewhere or put something on hold, let me ask later where it is and what I was supposed to do with it.
“I’m leaving—pack up what I’m doing so I can continue from the pendant, and pick it back up when I return.”
“Stay with me quietly in this conversation. When I ask you something, check my private notes and logged-in work pages, then whisper only a short, sourced answer through the pendant.”

“Can I take this on?” When I mention a new request or opportunity, compare it with my real commitments and deadlines, tell me the tradeoff in one short spoken answer, and—if it does not fit—draft a polite renegotiation or decline for my approval.

“Who was that person I just spoke with, and what should I remember for next time?” After I explicitly mark a conversation as worth remembering, identify the meeting or contact from my calendar/Mac, assemble a private relationship card from what was actually said plus clearly separated public context, and make it available from the pendant before my next interaction.

Before you brief me or act, tell me what is actually true across my pendant, Mac, browser, and relay—flag contradictions and stale status instead of confidently repeating them, and give me one safe next step to repair each problem.

When something I asked for goes wrong or arrives late, explain the incident in plain language—what I said, which surface received it, where it stalled, whether anything actually changed, and the safest retry—without repeating an action automatically.

Before I commit to something, let me rehearse the consequences: check my calendar, current commitments, private messages, travel or account details, and active browser work; show what this choice would collide with, what it would make harder, and a few safe alternatives—without changing anything.
Keep my pendant’s speech clear automatically as I move between a quiet room, a noisy street, and a Mac/browser call—without making me run a calibration each time.
If the pendant or relay is unsure what I said, catch the bad phrase before anything happens, ask me for only that phrase, and then continue the original request without making me start over.
Give me my briefing on the pendant, and keep it understandable and resumable even if the pendant is low on battery, the connection drops, or I get interrupted.
Keep me aware of genuinely urgent changes without making me pull out my phone or broadcasting private information in public; use a private signal now and explain it later.

“Make spoken replies and my queued briefings sound clear, but never let them stutter: use 24 kHz when the link and pendant can sustain it, fall back smoothly when they cannot, and resume at the exact sentence if I walk out of coverage.”
“Erase everything this hive knows about [topic/person/project] everywhere, prove what was erased, and stop any queued or offline action that depends on it.”
“Keep the pendant useful all day: spend battery and bandwidth on urgent things, defer or compress everything else, and tell me what was deferred before it becomes stale.”
“Handle it quietly, and only get my attention if you need me.”
“Before I commit to this, show me what it will cost me and what it will displace.”
If I miss something genuinely important, keep trying to reach me quietly, and—only under rules I set—escalate to a trusted person with exactly what happened.

When I’m carrying something out in the world, let me point the pendant at it and ask what I’m looking at or what to do next—read a label, find the right switch, compare two items, or follow a repair step hands-free.
“When a meeting ends, ask me what I actually decided, turn my answer into the right notes and follow-ups, draft any messages, and check back only if a commitment is still unresolved.”
“I just agreed to something—save the last minute as a private, sourced note, tell me what commitments you found, and let me correct them before you create reminders or drafts.”

“Before I commit to a purchase, booking, or cancellation, compare the logged-in options, check my calendar and existing commitments, explain the real trade-offs, and hold the best reversible draft until I approve.”

“Before I say yes to this invitation or request, tell me the true time, money, and attention cost against my existing commitments, then give me a one-sentence accept, decline, or counteroffer I can approve.”

“Read this message or draft before I send it as the other person would: point out ambiguity, accidental commitments, privacy leaks, and likely emotional impact, then show me two safer rewrites without sending anything.”

“When I tell you I am overloaded, find the smallest set of changes that makes today survivable: defer or reschedule reversible items, prepare concise decline messages, and leave me with one next action on the pendant.”
“If something on my calendar, in my inbox, or on a logged-in site changes, tell me what that change now affects and prepare the smallest set of fixes.”
“I’m with people” / “private mode”
“Hold this thought.” Later: “What was I in the middle of, and continue it.”
“Tell me when you hear a sound I care about—like the doorbell, smoke alarm, or my name—even if I’m wearing headphones or away from the Mac.”
“Let Alex help me with this for the next hour, but only give them what this task needs.”
“Before I choose, show me what each option would do to the rest of my week—without changing anything.”

When I say “I’ll handle that,” remember the commitment, watch the relevant calendar, mail, browser and local-file evidence, and nudge me only if it is still unresolved near the right time—with a one-tap pendant action to finish, defer, or dismiss it.

When I ask “what should I do?”, combine what my pendant heard, what is open in my private browser tabs, and what my Mac knows locally; give me three options with consequences and confidence, remember which I chose, and carry out only that option.

Before I enter an important conversation, quietly assemble a private “what I need to remember” card from my calendar, recent mail, notes, and relevant logged-in pages; let me ask the pendant for one fact at a time, and capture the decisions and follow-ups afterward.

When I am weighing a consequential choice, let me ask “what happens if I choose this?”, and show me a private, source-backed rehearsal of the next month: calendar collisions, likely messages, commitments I would break, costs or deadlines visible on my Mac, and the assumptions that could make the forecast wrong.

Help me preserve the meaning of a day, not just its files: when I say “save this moment,” combine a short pendant note with the nearby calendar event, open document or page, and my chosen feeling or lesson; months later I can ask what I learned and get a small, cited life story rather than a pile of transcripts.

Before I share something with a person or group, ask “what is safe to disclose here?” and produce three versions—a private full version, a bounded version, and a minimal version—using my actual documents and messages while preserving secrets and showing exactly which facts were omitted or generalized.
“I have 20 minutes. What is the one thing I should do now—and set it up for me?”
“Before I commit to this, show me what it will cost me next week.”
“I corrected you—make sure you stop using the old version everywhere.”
“Translate what they just said, and whisper the meaning to me without interrupting the conversation.”
“What am I actually agreeing to here? Give me the one risk and one question to ask before I say yes.”
“Once a month, tell me what keeps going wrong in my life-admin—and change one routine to make next month easier.”
“Before I submit this form or send this message, tell me exactly what personal information it would reveal, remove anything unnecessary, and let me approve the smallest safe version.”

“I’m about to leave. Based on what changed today, my calendar, and my open browser work, give me a five-minute departure plan: what I must take, who needs an update, and the one thing I should do first.”

“When I say ‘I can’t deal with this right now,’ put the current problem into a safe holding pattern: capture what it is, preserve the exact browser/Mac state, suggest a next reminder time, and give me one sentence I can use to explain the delay.”

“The meeting just ended. Turn what happened into the smallest useful follow-up: extract decisions and owners from my notes, compare them with the open threads in Mail and browser, draft the needed messages and reminders, and show me the send list.”

“Coordinate this with everyone without making me the middleman: find a time that works from the information I’m allowed to use, prepare each person a different message that reveals only what they need to know, and show me the complete coordination plan before anything is sent.”
“Translate this conversation as we go, quietly: tell me in my ear what the other person said, and give me a short translation of my reply before I say it.”

“When I tap the pendant during a meeting, remember that moment. Afterward, tell me the decisions, action items, and who owes what, with the exact audio/text evidence, then draft (but never send) the follow-ups.”

“Before any sensitive form, message, or purchase is submitted, show me exactly which fields will leave my browser, redact anything unnecessary, and let me approve the final payload with one physical pendant tap.”

“Teach me one useful personal shortcut each week: notice a repetitive sequence I approved across my Mac and browser, show me the proposed macro and its safety boundaries on the pendant, and install it only when I say yes.”

“When I tap the pendant while reading or listening, save the exact text or page fragment I’m on with a short voice annotation. Later, let me say ‘put that in my notes’ or ‘send that to this draft’ and insert the cited fragment into the right Mac or browser surface.”

“When two of my sources disagree—like Calendar versus an email or a browser reservation—do not silently pick one. Bring me a tiny conflict card with the competing evidence, what decision expires first, and one recommended resolution I can accept by voice.”

“Before I send or commit to something important, run a private adversarial check: wrong recipient, stale attachment, conflicting dates, suspicious payment details, or a promise I cannot keep. Show me only concrete risks and the evidence; do not change anything.”

When I say “I’m leaving” or “I’m on my way,” assemble a departure handoff: check my next calendar commitment, relevant logged-in travel or reservation tabs, unfinished Mac work, and anything I explicitly marked to bring up; give me one 20-second spoken checklist on the pendant and leave the full cited packet on my Mac. Never send or change anything.

Before I commit to a consequential choice, let me ask “what if I don’t do this?” Have the system compare the relevant calendar commitments, open browser obligations, reminders, and active projects, then give me a compact consequence map: what breaks, by when, who is affected, and what the least-cost alternative is. Do not take action.

Let me say a standing boundary such as “never send work mail after 8 pm” or “ask before opening financial pages,” then have the system turn it into a plain-language policy, test it against Mac, browser, relay, and pendant examples, and enforce it everywhere. If a case is ambiguous, ask me one question instead of guessing.

During a meeting, let me say “quiet coach.” The pendant should privately listen for questions or decisions, consult the relevant calendar event, open Mac documents, and authenticated browser tabs, then whisper a short suggested answer or say “I’m not sure.” After the meeting, leave a cited list of questions I could not answer. Never speak aloud to the room or send anything.

When I say “teach me this,” turn a topic from my current browser page, Mac document, or voice question into a private learning loop: explain it briefly, ask me one retrieval question through the pendant, adapt the next question to my answer, and bring it back days later until I can use it. Keep a small progress record instead of replaying the whole lesson.

Let me ask “what am I avoiding?” The system should inspect unfinished projects, repeatedly postponed reminders, stale browser tabs, unsent drafts, and calendar commitments, then return at most three avoidance hypotheses with evidence and one tiny reversible next step for each. It must distinguish lack of time, uncertainty, missing information, and unwillingness, and let me reject a hypothesis permanently.
“I’m leaving my desk—make sure I can pick up exactly where I am when I come back.”
“I was away—tell me only what changed while I was gone, and put the important things in order.”

entries.summary: “Give me a 25-minute focus sprint on this, and bring me back only if something truly urgent happens.”
“While I’m talking, quietly warn me if I’m about to promise something that conflicts with my calendar or existing commitments—never speak aloud unless I ask.”
“I have about 40 minutes and low energy—choose one useful thing I can realistically finish, set it up, and stop me from starting something too big.”
“When I’m reading something important, check the claims against independent sources and quietly flag what is uncertain or out of date.”

“Before, during, and after my meetings, keep me from losing the thread: brief me from Calendar and the relevant logged-in tabs, let me tap the pendant to capture decisions and commitments offline, then reconcile those captures with the meeting notes on my Mac and prepare reminders or drafts for my review.”

“When you answer a factual question about my accounts, machine, schedule, or browser, tell me whether the evidence is fresh and sufficient; if it is stale, contradictory, or a permission-blocked guess, say so in one sentence and offer the smallest next check instead of pretending.”

“Give me a private, one-button 'where I left off' capsule: from the pendant, resume the last unfinished conversation or Mac/browser job with its goal, what was actually completed, what failed, and the single safest next action—without replaying anything.”

“Let me use the pendant as a private control surface in public: acknowledge that you heard me, tell me silently whether you are thinking, need my approval, or failed, and let me cancel before anything consequential happens—without speaking sensitive details aloud.”

When I tap the pendant and say “save this,” preserve exactly what I was looking at and thinking about: the current Mac app, selected browser tab and page excerpt, a short audio note, and a suggested next action; later say “show me my saves” and let me resume one.
When you answer a question using my private browser or Mac, let me say “why?” and hear the exact source chain in one sentence, then open the same tab and highlight the supporting text on my Mac.

When my calendar, email, and a logged-in website disagree about a commitment, tell me there is a conflict, name the two competing facts, and ask one precise question on the pendant; after I answer, update the plan and leave an audit trail instead of silently choosing.

Forget what I just said everywhere: remove the pendant recording, transcript, cached audio, derived notes, browser extracts, and Mac job context, then tell me exactly what was deleted and what could not be reached.

Put the pendant and Mac into guest mode for the next hour: answer general questions, but do not read my mail, calendar, browser sessions, saved notes, or personal memory, and give me a receipt when private mode is restored.
“When I say approve, show me the exact action on my Mac, then let me confirm it with one deliberate tap on the pendant—only after that may you send, buy, delete, or submit.”
“If my pendant is lost or I hold its button for five seconds, lock down my private sessions everywhere and erase any queued recordings or spoken briefings; tell me what was revoked when I recover.”

“When I arrive somewhere or start a focused block, make my devices agree on the same privacy mode: hush non-urgent pendant audio, pause browser watchers, defer Mac notifications, and give me one short catch-up when I leave.”
“Know when I am still wearing the pendant: lock my Mac’s private browser sessions and stop sensitive audio when it is set down, then restore my place when I put it back on.”
“When I am in a conversation, let me say ‘mark that’ and have the pendant save only the next ten seconds of speech locally, then ask whether to keep, transcribe, or erase it when I am alone.”
“Before I leave home, tell me what I am likely to forget based on today’s calendar and the things I normally carry, but only interrupt me when the confidence is high.”

“Run my monthly access-resilience check: verify that my important accounts, backups, browser sessions, Mac, and pendant can still be recovered, and tell me exactly what would fail—without exposing any secrets or changing anything.”
“Audit my privacy across the pendant, relay, Mac, and logged-in browser: show me what sensitive material is stored where, who can reach it, and give me a safe, reversible cleanup plan.”

“When I tap the pendant at the start and end of a conversation, securely capture that interval, transcribe it on my Mac, and leave me a private summary of decisions, names, and follow-ups—never record outside the two taps.”

“Make my pendant a physical privacy key: when I tap it near my Mac, unlock my private AI session and browser workspace; when I tap again or walk away, freeze the session, mute capture, and hide sensitive tabs.”

“If I hold the pendant button for five seconds, start a private safety check-in: tell me whether my Mac, relay, and wearable are reachable, and if I do not cancel within a minute, send my chosen contact a prewritten message with my last known location and status.”

“Create a temporary, least-privilege handoff for this task: give my collaborator only the selected files, links, decision history, and next step, then revoke the link automatically when the task is closed or expires.”
“Show me what you’re about to send or change, and let me approve it with one press on my pendant.”
“When did I decide this, and what evidence led me there?”
“I got interrupted—give me the one-minute context I need to continue, and put me back where I was.”
“Warn me before my personal information leaves my devices, wherever I’m about to send it.”
“Watch me do this once, then offer to handle the boring parts next time without taking over.”
“The meeting just ended—turn what happened into follow-through.”
“Before I meet someone, remind me who they are and what I owe them—without making me search.”
“I’m stuck. Look at what I’m doing and give me one concrete next move, then do the reversible part.”
“Help me learn what actually gives me energy or drains me, without turning my life into a surveillance dashboard.”
“Keep an emergency packet for the person I choose, so if I’m unreachable they know what matters—but never give anyone my whole digital life.”
“When I’m about to say yes to something important, show me the real cost to my time and commitments before I agree.”
“Keep an eye on the commitments I care about, and warn me only when something genuinely threatens them.”
“Before I commit to this, show me what it will break, what it will postpone, and the least disruptive way to do it.”
“Put me in work mode, and make sure nothing from my personal life leaks into work—or comes back the other way.”
“Why did I decide to do this?” Then, when I revisit a project, remind me of the short voice note I left about the decision and show the files, calendar event, or private web page that informed it.

“Teach me how to do this once, then let me do the next one.” Have the Mac or browser perform the first safe example while the pendant explains each meaningful step, then hand me the next instance and check my result before I submit anything.

“What am I looking at, and what is the next safe step?” Have the pendant give me a concise spoken explanation of the currently focused Mac window or browser tab, identify the relevant controls or missing information, and offer one reversible next action—without changing anything until I say go.

Tell me when two parts of you disagree about reality—for example, when a surface says it is ready but cannot perform its advertised operation, or when a job is complete in one store and unfinished in another—and show me the smallest test that would resolve the disagreement.

Erase this piece of private content everywhere you stored or derived it, and show me a deletion receipt listing every store checked, every copy removed or tombstoned, and any copy you could not reach.

"Is the system's picture of the world internally consistent right now?" Give me contradictions such as a stale timezone, a device claimed online by one surface but absent from the registry, or a browser action with no matching receipt, with source, age, and confidence for every side.

"Why did you think that was true when you acted?" Show me a time-ordered evidence replay for one claim or action: what the relay, Mac, browser, and (when present) pendant each reported at the decision time, what was missing, and which later observation proved or contradicted it.

"Before you act, give me a fresh witness certificate; after you act, prove the state changed." For any consequential request, require independent witnesses for the target and authorization, then perform a bounded postcondition check across the relevant surface and return pass, fail, or unknown—not a guessed success.

"What happened in the right order while you were disconnected?" Reconstruct a tamper-evident event sequence spanning pendant-offline speech, relay conversations, Mac actions, and browser changes, using sequence continuity and later time anchors; show relative order when wall-clock time is unknowable instead of inventing timestamps.

"How many independent witnesses actually know this—not how many copies repeat it?" For any important claim, show the evidence-dependency graph, collapse mirrored reports from the same source, and tell me whether confidence comes from one origin or genuinely independent observations.

"Can I trust the device that reported this?" Verify the identity and software provenance of the pendant, Mac bridge, relay, and browser extension for each evidence-bearing answer, flag unexpected firmware/build or extension changes, and quarantine observations from an untrusted component.

entries.note: briefing.js: morning brief reads Calendar+Mail+recent files+Mac state, flags meetings needing prep, derives a priority list; spoken line + long-form audio + Notes.app note + markdown. Live-verified on the owner's real calendar/inbox.

entries.summary: “Clean up my Downloads every Friday: group files by project, rename obvious duplicates, and show me a review list before anything is deleted.”
entries.note: Duplicate of cap-0e0b8d35 + cap-52dcc328, both implemented in downloadsTidy.js: the Friday schedule, the dated grouping and the review-before-anything list are all there. Its two extra words are answered rather than skipped — duplicates are detected by content signature and REPORTED, never renamed or deleted, because 'obvious duplicate' is a guess and deletion is not reversible.

entries.summary: “Research this topic and leave me a concise source-linked briefing on my Mac, with an audio version I can play later.”
entries.note: local-agent/audioBrief.js deliverBriefing(): every run leaves BOTH a source-linked markdown note and a .wav/.opus pair with the same basename under ~/AI-Pendant-Workspace/Briefings. Audio is rendered at the pendant's exact wire format (24 kHz mono s16le + Ogg Opus) so it plays on the Mac or from the pendant later; ceiling is 120 s, not the 10 s reply cap. Verified: 71-85 s briefs produced.

entries.summary: “Every morning, give me a concise briefing of today’s calendar, unread priority messages, weather, and the files I need for my first meeting; let me ask follow-ups and open anything I mention.”
entries.note: Covered by briefing.js kind=morning (same brief as cap-fb442a50): today's calendar, priority vs bulk unread mail, recent files, Mac state. Two parts of the ask are NOT built: weather is not folded in (get_weather exists as a separate action), and 'the files I need for my first meeting' is a recency list, not per-meeting file matching. Follow-ups/'open anything I mention' are the normal conversational path, not this module.

entries.summary: “Prepare me for my next meeting: find the agenda and related local documents, summarize the open decisions and prior action items, and put the three most relevant files in a folder I can open.”
entries.note: meetingPrep.js. Retrieval, not summary: ranks local documents against the invite and quotes the sentences that already state a decision or an action, with their source file. Two bugs found and fixed against the owner's real data — a 5-minute solo alarm was being treated as 'the next meeting', and the organiser's own name matched every file on the machine. Verified live: found the real 9pm interview, 3 related documents copied into a folder with BRIEF.md. GET /meeting-prep. 14 tests.

entries.summary: “When I say ‘prepare my workday’, check my calendar and inbox, make a concise brief, and put it in a note on my Mac; don't send anything.”
entries.note: briefing.js kind=workday: 'prepare my workday' matches deterministically (no model call), reads Calendar+Mail, writes a Notes.app note and a markdown brief. Composes and stores only — assertNeverSends refuses any transmitting sink and there is no transport call in the module.

entries.summary: “Find the best flight options for next Thursday, compare total price and duration, and leave me a shortlist; do not book.”
entries.note: research.js (another agent, in this round) already is this capability: mode 'compare' gathers and verifies sources, and 'do not book' is structural there — no code path transacts, and assertNoTransactionClaim throws if the model even narrates a booking. Verified by running the actual flight query through POST /research: it returned a real nonstop-vs-connecting comparison for next Thursday with no booking. A second flight-specific ranker would duplicate it.

entries.summary: “Clean up my Downloads: group files by type into folders and show me what will be moved before doing it.”
entries.note: downloadsTidy.js. Preview and apply are two calls with the plan persisted between them, so apply replays exactly what the owner read rather than recomputing it; sources are re-stat'd and anything that changed is reported as drift and skipped. Nothing deletes, collisions are suffixed, every apply leaves an undo manifest. Verified against the owner's real ~/Downloads: 28 files previewed into 5 groups, NOTHING APPLIED. 16 tests.

entries.summary: “Every weekday at 5 pm, summarize the notes I created today into three next actions and put them in my task app; never send messages.”
entries.note: briefing.js kind=wrapup + a daily 17:00 routine via routines.js: summarizes notes created today into <=3 next actions and creates real macOS Reminders. Never sends. Fixed a live feedback loop where it followed up on its own briefing notes.

entries.summary: “Give me a workday brief at 8:30, and let me play it from the pendant when I’m ready.”
entries.note: Same brief as cap-1634d96f with a clock and a speaker bolted on, and both parts already exist: routines.js schedules it at 08:30 and audioBrief.js/briefing.js render and play it on the pendant. Nothing here needs new machinery — building a second day-brief would mean two things to keep in sync.

entries.summary: “Before my next meeting, prepare me: open the agenda, summarize relevant email, and put a private briefing on the pendant.”
entries.note: Duplicate of cap-0fee609c, which is implemented in meetingPrep.js: same agenda, same related-mail search, same folder of documents. The one difference — 'a private briefing on the pendant' — is audioBrief.js's job, and meetingPrep already returns a spoken summary for it to render.

entries.summary: “Research this topic, compare the best options, and leave me a short audio recommendation—don’t buy anything.”
entries.note: mode=compare: compares real options and ends with one recommendation plus what would change it. 'Don't buy anything' is built in, not a gate — no code path here can transact, the compose prompt forbids claiming otherwise, and assertNoTransactionClaim() rejects a brief that says it ordered/booked/paid (tested). The note states 'Nothing was bought, booked or ordered'. Verified live on portable power stations under $500.

Unread mail is classified into urgent / reply soon / reference / noise, replies are drafted for the first two, and the whole thing is written to ~/AI-Pendant-Workspace/mail-triage/<run>/REVIEW.md with one file per draft. Four classification bugs found and fixed against that real inbox: Hide My Email relays read as people, a bulk DOMAIN was being read as a marketing SENDER, and role addresses plus brand display names ('Valerie from Holafly', 'Premium*Tesla <Sales.SG@...>') earned drafted replies to adverts.
