entries.summary: When I say 'clean up my desktop', group obvious screenshots and downloads into dated folders, but show me the proposed moves first.
entries.note: local-agent/folderSweep.js: surveyFolder / planSweep / formatSweep / applySweep / undoSweep, plus GET /sweep/survey, POST /sweep/preview, GET /sweep[/:planId], POST /sweep/:planId/apply, POST /sweep/:planId/undo, and the sweep_folder_preview / _apply / _undo action types. Real classification, not a name-based guess: half-finished downloads (.crdownload/.part/.tmp/~$ and zero-byte files at least a day old, so nothing mid-write is touched), byte-identical duplicates (size + 64 KB sample to find candidates, then a full sha256 to settle it, capped at 256 MB above which the match is reported as unconfirmed and never proposed for deletion), stale installers (with an /Applications lookup so it can say "cursor is already installed"), stale files, and screenshots. Dispositions: delete / archive / file / flag / keep. Duplicates are only proposed for deletion when the bytes are proven identical AND the name reads as a copy ("report (1).pdf" beside "report.pdf"); anything that merely shares content is reported and left alone. Destinations are resolved to a free name at preview time, so nothing is ever overwritten and the path the owner reads is the path the file lands at. THE PREVIEW ON THE OWNER REAL DESKTOP, live through the running agent: 588 loose files, 556 screenshots and screen recordings totalling ~10 GB proposed into Screenshots/YYYY-MM/, 27 stale files into Archive/YYYY-MM/, 5 left alone. Nothing was applied. That preview also found a real bug: this Mac names screenshots in Traditional Chinese, and 30-odd files called "截圖 ..." were being filed as merely stale - SCREENSHOT_NAME now covers zh/ja/ko/es/fr/de/ru/nl as well as English, which is the sort of thing only real files tell you. NOT a gate: applySweep never asks anything, there is no token or expiry on a plan (a test asserts that), and move_path/delete_path still run immediately through /execute exactly as before. Apply takes a planId because "do what you showed me" is only meaningful if the thing applied is the thing shown; it re-checks every source against the recorded size and mtime and reports drift rather than substituting a fresh guess, and it runs through the ordinary executor so each item leaves a receipt and an undo-vault snapshot. 18 node:test cases.

entries.summary: Clean up my Downloads: identify duplicate, temporary, and likely finished files, show me a proposed plan, then move only the approved items into an archive folder.
entries.note: Same module as cap-2eef696b: local-agent/folderSweep.js + the /sweep routes + sweep_folder_preview/_apply. This entry is the one that asked for all four parts by name, and all four are there. IDENTIFY: duplicate (size + 64 KB sample to shortlist, full sha256 to confirm, 256 MB cap above which it is reported unconfirmed and never deleted), temporary (.crdownload/.part/.partial/.download/.tmp/.aria2/~$ plus zero-byte files at least a day old), and likely finished (stale by mtime, default 90 days; stale installers at 30, with an /Applications lookup that says whether the app is already installed). SHOW ME A PROPOSED PLAN: POST /sweep/preview writes the plan and returns it with a formatted preview; nothing moves. MOVE ONLY THE APPROVED ITEMS: POST /sweep/:planId/apply takes an "only" list of item ids, so the owner who read twelve lines and wants three gets three - a selection, not a permission; naming an id that is not in the plan is an error rather than a fresh decision. INTO AN ARCHIVE FOLDER: Archive/YYYY-MM/ (Installers/ subfolder for those), Screenshots/YYYY-MM/ for captures. LIVE ON THE OWNER REAL ~/Downloads, preview only, nothing applied: 28 loose files, no duplicates, 3 screenshots from July proposed into Screenshots/2026-07/, 24 active files correctly left alone at the 90-day default. At a 21-day threshold it also picks up Cursor-darwin-universal.dmg (410 MB) with the reason "cursor is already in /Applications; installer last touched 10 days ago". The restraint is the point: an agent that moved all 28 would have been wrong. Not a gate - applySweep asks nothing, holds no token, and every direct file action still executes immediately.

entries.summary: “Once a week, clean up my Downloads: group files by type and project, flag duplicates and stale installers, and show me a review list before anything is deleted.”
entries.note: Covered by local-agent/folderSweep.js (see cap-2b03a27d), with the two parts this entry adds that nothing else had. FLAG DUPLICATES AND STALE INSTALLERS: downloadsTidy.js already reported duplicates, but had no notion of an installer going stale; classifyFile now tags installer / stale-installer / already-installed by checking /Applications, which on the owner real Downloads produced "cursor is already in /Applications; installer last touched 10 days ago" for a 410 MB dmg. A REVIEW LIST BEFORE ANYTHING IS DELETED: the delete section of the preview is separated from the move sections and each line carries its reason, and deletes go through the executor so each one is snapshotted into the undo vault first and undoSweep puts the bytes back - verified by a test that deletes a .crdownload and restores it. GROUP BY TYPE: yes, via the disposition classes and downloadsTidy planTidy groupBy=type/date. GROUP BY PROJECT: NOT BUILT - inferring which project a loose download belongs to needs projectMemory/contextGraph and is a different piece of work; nothing here guesses at it. ONCE A WEEK: the scheduler already exists (routines.js + POST /routines), and sweep_folder_preview is a plannable action type, so a weekly routine can be created without new code; no routine was created, since standing configuration on the owner machine is theirs to set up. Overlaps cap-0e0b8d35 / cap-b4dfb9ea / cap-52dcc328, which another subagent took for the group-by-type/date half in downloadsTidy.js; this entry is filed implemented rather than duplicate because the duplicate-confidence, stale-installer and review-before-delete parts are only in folderSweep.js.

“Keep me focused: watch my Mac and logged-in browser notifications, suppress routine noise, and tell me on the pendant only when something genuinely urgent needs me.”

“When the pendant hits a hardware or audio fault, file a useful bug report for me automatically.”

When I say “bookmark this moment,” save what I’m looking at and saying so I can later say “resume that” from the pendant and have the Mac reopen the exact browser/app context and read me the short handoff.

When I say “leave this here,” preserve a resumable work capsule across my pendant, Mac, and browser: the spoken intent, the exact authenticated tab or app state, relevant local files, and the next safe step. When I later say “pick up where I left off,” restore the context and continue from that checkpoint without repeating my research.
“Keep the conversation intact even when the cellular link is struggling—prioritize my speech, recover anything that was lost, and tell me plainly if something could not be recovered.”
“If something I asked you to do can’t run right now, keep it safely queued, tell me what’s blocked, and finish it automatically when the Mac or browser comes back.”

“Give me a physical privacy button: when I press it, stop all AI watching and automation everywhere, close or blur any AI-opened sensitive views, and tell me what was retained—without losing my unfinished work.”
“Why couldn't you do that, and fix whatever is preventing it if you can?”
During a meeting, when I say “mark that,” capture the moment and later give me a sourced follow-up list.

When I enter a meeting, quietly put the whole hive into meeting-safe mode: suppress nonessential pendant interruptions, pause background browser actions, hide sensitive Mac windows and notifications, and restore everything when the meeting ends—while still allowing an urgent alert through.
“Make the pendant sound as clear as possible, and keep it clear when the connection is bad.”
“Let me move between my pendant and Mac without restarting the conversation—continue speaking on whichever device I’m using, and keep the same context and audio state.”
“Let me keep talking naturally while I’m walking—even when LTE gets busy—and recover any dropped words without making me repeat myself.”
“Give me a protected 45 minutes.”
“I lost the pendant—protect everything and help me get back in.”
“When I’m in a meeting, keep interruptions quiet; collect anything important and give me a two-minute catch-up when it ends.”
“Save where I am, and when I come back, put me back into this task exactly as I left it.”
“Save my place here.” Later: “Resume the thing I saved.”
“Fill this in with my saved details, but don’t show the private values to the AI or speak them aloud.”
“If my Mac or browser is unavailable, tell me what you last verified, how stale it is, and keep my task ready to resume when the device comes back.”
“I need this ready by [time]; do the highest-value parts first across my Mac and logged-in browser, and give me a useful partial result if anything is blocked.”
“When the pendant audio sounds bad, diagnose the whole path and fix the best thing automatically.”
“Start this now; if anything can't run, keep the rest moving and tell me exactly what finished, what's waiting, and what I need to fix.”
“Use my private tabs and local files to answer this, but keep the raw contents on my Mac—send only the minimum redacted evidence needed, and show me what left the device.”

When I ask from the pendant to do something across my Mac and logged-in browser, keep the task coherent if either one disconnects, never duplicate a completed step, and tell me exactly what ran, what did not, and what was verified when it is finished.
“Keep working on this even if my Mac or browser disconnects, tell me exactly what is blocked, and resume automatically when it is safe.”
“If the Mac gets stuck while I’m away, tell me what you need on the pendant, let me answer there, and continue the same job without making me reopen the Mac.”

When I ask you to do something on my Mac, tell me truthfully whether it actually happened—and if the Mac cannot act, keep trying through the right surface and give me a useful fallback instead of claiming success.

After I finish a conversation, turn the commitments I just made into a short follow-up queue: draft the emails, calendar changes, and authenticated browser updates on my Mac, then let me review and send or apply each one from the pendant.

When I say “I’m presenting” (or press the pendant button), hide distracting Mac/browser interruptions for this meeting, keep only genuinely urgent alerts reachable through the pendant, and restore everything afterward with a concise missed-items summary.

When I press the pendant twice and say “private moment,” make the whole hive safe to use around other people: the Mac and browser should hide notification previews and sensitive tab content, the relay should speak only minimal status, and pressing again should restore my exact prior state and show me what was suppressed.

If I tell you to do something later, queue it safely: when my Mac or logged-in browser comes back, re-check that the request is still relevant, do it if the preconditions hold, and tell me on the pendant exactly what happened. If it has gone stale or would send/delete/buy, stop and ask me.

Hand this conversation from my pendant to my Mac without making me repeat myself. When I tap twice, preserve the last few spoken turns and the relevant browser/app context, open a private continuation on the Mac, and let me continue there; when I leave, let me hand it back to the pendant as a short spoken summary.
“If I ask you to do something while my browser or Mac is unavailable, remember it safely, tell me what is waiting, and finish it when the right device comes back—without acting on stale information.”
“For this request, keep my data local—or let it use the browser and relay—and prove afterward exactly where the data went.”
When I ask for my inbox, GitHub, or calendar, give me what is available now and finish the rest automatically when the browser comes back.
Continue the thing I was doing yesterday, from where I left off, and show me the next action before you do it.
“Park this exactly where it is; when I say resume later, put me back in the same work and tell me what changed.”
“If you’re carrying out a long task on my Mac or in Safari, let me interrupt you from the pendant at any moment; stop cleanly, preserve exactly what was done, and tell me what remains.”
“Close out my 2pm meeting.”
“I’m back at my desk—tell me only what changed since I left, and put the things I need to act on in front of me.”

“Can you handle this on my computer?” — before acting, tell me which surfaces are actually available, use the best available route, and if something is unavailable, keep working with a degraded plan and tell me exactly what remains.

“Do this when it won’t interrupt me.” Let the pendant capture the request, the relay understand my current interruption policy, and the Mac wait for a safe moment—such as not presenting, not in a call, and not typing—before carrying out the desktop work, then tell me what happened.
“I’m going into a meeting—keep everything quiet, but don’t lose anything important, and resume my work when it’s over.”
“Prepare all of this across my Mac and logged-in browser, but don’t change the real world until I approve one complete preview—and if I approve, apply it as one recoverable transaction.”
Make my Mac ready for automation, and tell me when it is working.
Make sure this actually gets done: keep the commitment with me, notice whether I completed it across my Mac and logged-in browser, and nudge me on the pendant only if it is still unfinished.
“Handle this browser task even if the browser bridge is asleep; wake the right browser, resume when it is available, and tell me exactly where it stopped if it cannot recover.”
“I have to leave—save exactly where I am, keep the private details on my Mac, and let me resume this same task from the pendant or another device later without starting over.”

“Even when my browser is closed or offline, answer questions about the private pages I previously chose to make available—tell me exactly when the information was captured, show the source link and evidence, and tell me when it may be stale.”

“Continue what I’m looking at.” The pendant should identify the owner’s current Mac document, browser page, selected text, and relevant window state, then let them continue that exact thread by voice or have the Mac prepare the next step without making them explain or share a screenshot.
When I press and hold the pendant, hide sensitive work everywhere immediately; when I release and authenticate again, restore exactly what I was doing.
When something fails, say “file this failure” and leave a privacy-safe bug report with the exact Mac/browser/pendant evidence and the next recovery step.

When I walk away from my Mac, remember what I was doing across my open apps and logged-in browser tabs; when I come back and say “pick up where I left off,” give me the shortest useful re-entry brief and restore only the relevant workspace.
Park this and let me pick it up later.
Privacy curtain on.
What left my devices for that task?

“Even if my Mac or browser is offline, remember this browser task, tell me it’s queued, and do it when the right tab comes back—unless the page or request has gone stale.”

When I say “resume where I left off,” reconstruct my last interrupted work session across the Mac and authenticated browser: reopen the relevant files and tabs, recover the unsent draft or pending form without submitting it, summarize what was completed and what remains, and let me continue from the pendant.

“Save my place here, and bring me back to this exact work later.”

When I’m about to leave my Mac or Wi‑Fi, let me say “pack me for the day,” and give me a private offline day pack on the pendant: my next commitments, essential addresses/links, files I chose, and a short spoken summary that I can query while disconnected; sync any notes I make back to the Mac when I return.

“Finish the thing I started earlier, and tell me only if you’re blocked.” The system should reconcile my pending Mac and browser work, resume safe steps when the right surface returns, and give me one short pendant update.

“What do I need to know before my 2 pm meeting?” The system should privately join my Calendar, Mail, local notes/files, and authenticated browser pages on the Mac, return a concise answer through the pendant, and show exactly which sources were used without uploading their contents to the relay.
“If you can’t safely verify a Mac or browser action, tell me what is blocked, leave a resumable task, and finish it automatically when the right device comes back.”
“Continue this on my pendant from where I left off on the Mac—read the selected page or document aloud, let me interrupt with a question, and resume at the same paragraph later.”
“Remember this for me, and let me get back to the exact place later.”
I'm heading out—check whether I’m going to be late or forget anything, and leave me a short spoken checklist on the pendant.
Before I send or upload this, check that it is going to the right person/site and that I am not accidentally exposing anything sensitive.

When a meeting is 10 minutes away, get me ready: summarize the event and relevant mail, gather context from my already-open work tabs, save what I was doing, and after it ends restore my workspace and give me the follow-ups.
If I lose connection, quit the wrong app, or a browser form is about to disappear, warn me and save a private recovery capsule so I can say 'restore what I was doing' from the pendant later.
“Pause this and save my place. Later, resume it exactly where I left off.”
“Tell me what needs attention, but don’t say anything private out loud.”
“Find the exact thing I’m talking about and put it in front of me—don’t guess if there’s more than one.”
“If I start a task by voice and walk away or the connection gets bad, keep doing the safe parts on my Mac/browser and tell me on the pendant when it is ready for review.”

“If my Mac crashes, sleeps, or I accidentally close something, reconstruct what I was doing from my open documents, browser tabs, and recent pendant conversation, then restore a safe working set and tell me what could not be recovered.”
“Undo the last thing you did for me, across the Mac, browser, and any drafts or reminders, and show me exactly what was restored.”
“Save my current work so I can pick it up later.” Then, when I say “resume my saved work,” bring back the right browser tabs and Mac files and give me a short spoken orientation.

“Privacy mode.” When I enter a meeting or shared space, immediately hide sensitive Mac windows, pause authenticated browser work, and stop private spoken output; when I say “resume privately,” restore the exact working state and give me the missed updates discreetly through the pendant.

“Start this here, finish it wherever you can, and if anything disconnects, pick up exactly where you left off.” For example: gather the details from my logged-in browser tabs, make a draft in a Mac workspace folder, and leave a short spoken completion or recovery note on the pendant.

“Use my private browser tabs and Mac files to answer this, but keep the raw contents on my devices.” Return only the minimum facts, redacted excerpts, and verifiable citations needed for the answer or draft.
“Handle this private account task, but keep the page contents and anything I type on my Mac. Tell me only what you need me to know and ask before the final change.”
When my browser reconnects, tell me what was waiting and resume only the task I choose.
Bookmark this workspace, and restore it when I come back.
“If my browser disconnects, pause any private web task safely; when it reconnects, tell me what is stale and let me resume only the steps I choose.”
“When I leave my Mac halfway through something, give me a private handoff I can resume from the pendant later—what I was doing, what is unfinished, and the exact next safe step.”

If I tell you to handle something in Safari and then my laptop or Wi‑Fi drops, keep the task safe: prepare what you can, pause if the page/session changed, and tell me from the pendant exactly what is waiting before anything is submitted.
I have to go—save my place everywhere and bring me back to exactly what I was doing when I return.
Go private for the next hour: keep helping me, but do not send anything from this task to the cloud, and tell me when a step cannot be done locally.
“If the browser is unavailable, do the safe equivalent on the Mac when possible; otherwise keep my request until the browser returns, then tell me exactly what happened.”
“If I get interrupted, save this task and continue it later from the exact next safe step—across my pendant, Mac, and browser—without repeating anything or losing the result.”

If something I asked depends on my Mac or a logged-in browser that is unavailable, keep working with whatever evidence is already cached, tell me exactly what is blocked, and resume automatically when that surface comes back.

Let me start a conversation on the pendant, continue it on my Mac without repeating myself, and then send the final answer back to the pendant—even if LTE drops briefly or I switch between speaking and typing.

“If the pendant, Mac agent, or browser bridge stops working, figure out what failed, collect the smallest useful evidence, and leave me one plain-language recovery card; tell me only when it needs me.”

“When I press the pendant button at the start and end of a meeting, keep a private meeting packet: identify the agenda and attendees from my calendar and open work tabs, capture only the notes I explicitly mark, then leave me decisions, action items with owners and dates, and unsent follow-up drafts.”
“If something I asked you to do got stuck, silently verify what really happened, quarantine any stale browser action, and tell me exactly what needs my one decision.”

“Save this exact moment for later.” Then, days later: “Resume the thing I saved,” and bring back the right page, file, and short explanation of what I was trying to do—without making any change on my behalf.
“Compare the document open on my Mac with the policy in my logged-in browser, and tell me only the clauses that differ, with the exact source for each difference. Do not edit either one.”
“I’m stepping away—save where I am. When I come back, put me back into this work and tell me the next three things.”

“Before I leave for an appointment, check my private calendar, recent mail, and logged-in reservation pages against each other; tell me only if the details conflict, and prepare a corrected itinerary I can review.”
“Before my next meeting, get me ready; after it ends, leave me the follow-ups.”
“Only interrupt me when something is important enough to break my focus; otherwise queue it and catch me at the next good moment.”
“Use my private browser tabs and Mac files to answer this, but keep the private material on my Mac and tell me exactly what crossed the boundary.”

Pause this and let me continue later. When I say “continue,” restore the exact work context across my pendant, Mac, and logged-in browser, tell me what changed while I was away, and resume only the next safe step.

Put this task in a private workroom. Use only the tabs, files, messages, and calendar items relevant to it; keep everything else out of context, show me what you included, and erase the workroom when I say “close it.”
If my browser or Mac is offline, queue the task safely, tell me when it comes back, and never execute a stale browser action without letting me cancel or restate it from the pendant.

When I double-press the pendant before I walk away, put my Mac and logged-in browser into privacy pause, stop any spoken output, and when I return let me unlock and resume only the work that was safely paused.
“Bookmark where I am. When I say resume that thread later, put me back exactly where I left off and remind me what I was doing.”
“If something you’re doing for me breaks halfway through, fix what can be fixed, put everything back to the last safe checkpoint, and tell me exactly what I need to decide.”
“Pick up where I left off on the Mac.” Later: “Resume that.”
“Stop everything and protect my data.” (A physical pendant gesture, even if the Mac screen is locked.)
“I’m switching tasks—make me a handoff packet.”
“Are my plans still valid?”

"Give me a current handoff packet." From the pendant, capture what is happening across my day right now: today's calendar and unread mail, the important content in my already-open authenticated browser tabs, and the Mac workspace I'm currently using. Redact sensitive fields, rank only items needing attention, leave a cited packet on the Mac, and queue a short spoken summary back to the pendant.

"Is anything inconsistent?" Have the system continuously reconcile my current Calendar, unread Mail, already-open authenticated browser tabs, and the Mac files or notes relevant to my active project. Tell me only when two sources disagree or a deadline/status has silently changed, explain the evidence side by side, and prepare a local correction plan without changing or sending anything.
Pause what you’re doing on my Mac and continue it later—even if I close the laptop; when I say resume, tell me what changed and pick up without repeating work.

Save this moment for me: keep the page I’m on, the relevant draft or selection, and why I cared, then let me reopen the same private workspace from the pendant later; erase it automatically after I’m done.
Before you use my private Mac or logged-in browser, tell me exactly what information would leave the device, let me remove any fields by voice, and then do the task with the redacted version.
Keep my pendant conversation clear when the LTE-M connection gets crowded, and return to full-quality 24 kHz audio automatically when it recovers.
When I interrupt you or the connection drops during a spoken answer, preserve the unfinished turn and let me resume it later from the pendant or Mac without repeating myself.

When I start talking over the pendant's reply, stop or duck it immediately, understand my interruption as a correction or new request, and continue with the right response without making me repeat myself.

“Do this when I’m free”: stage the browser/Mac work now, wait for a real interruption-safe gap, then carry it out and tell me on the pendant exactly what happened; let me cancel it with one button press.

“I’m leaving the Mac—package this exactly so I can resume it from the pendant later.” Preserve the current Mac app/document state, authenticated browser tabs, unsent drafts, evidence, and next safe step; let me ask the pendant what is waiting and resume or abandon it when I return.

“Before you use my Mac or logged-in browser, show me exactly what private data will leave each device, what will stay local, and let me say ‘redact that’ or ‘local only.’ Then proceed with the least-data version and give me a receipt afterward.”
“If that multi-step task partly failed, figure out exactly what changed, what did not, and repair only the missing pieces—without repeating anything that already happened.”

When I say “save this for later” while I’m looking at a page, capture the page and my spoken note as a sourced, searchable research card; later I can ask the pendant what I saved and have the Mac reopen the exact source.

Tell me before my important logged-in browser sessions expire or get signed out, and when I’m back at the Mac, open only the affected sign-in pages so I can restore them without exposing page contents.

When a meeting, deadline, or reservation changes in one place, tell me what other commitments it breaks and prepare the coordinated cleanup across my Mac, browser, and pendant—updated calendar details, draft notifications, and the exact tabs/files to close or reopen.
“I lost connection—resume the task I was doing and tell me exactly what is left.”
“Switch me to work mode” (or “personal mode”) and keep every action, tab, file, and spoken briefing in the right context.

If I say “pause that” or press the pendant button while a Mac/browser task is running, stop safely, save exactly where it got to, and let me say “resume it” later—even after the browser reconnects or the Mac was asleep.

After you do something important for me—send a message, change a record, submit a form, or create an appointment—prove that it actually took effect and tell me if the result is confirmed, contradicted, or unknown.

“If I start a multi-step task and then close my laptop or lose the browser, keep the work safe, resume it when the right device returns, and tell me exactly what was completed, skipped, or still needs me.”
“I’m leaving my desk—freeze this work exactly where it is, and when I come back, restore the useful parts and remind me what I was doing.”
“When you finish something for me, tell me at the first moment I can actually absorb it—not while I’m presenting or driving—and escalate only if it is genuinely time-critical.”
“Keep an eye on my important things, but only interrupt me when it’s genuinely urgent and I’m at a safe stopping point.”
“If my Mac loses Wi‑Fi, keep only my essential work connected through the pendant until normal internet returns.”
“If you lose connection while working on something, keep the work safe and resume it exactly once when my Mac or browser comes back—then tell me what was completed, skipped, or still needs me.”
“Tell me when my Mac, browser, and pendant disagree about whether something happened, and help me reconcile it without repeating the action.”
“Start this multi-step task and keep it safe if the browser, Mac, or connection drops—resume where you left off and tell me exactly what completed, what did not, and what needs me.”
“Prepare this for me, but make the approval expire if anything important changes—tell me exactly what changed instead of letting stale work go through.”
Keep my private browser work reliable: if the browser bridge drops or has stuck commands, recover what can be recovered, tell me what was not run, and never silently replay a risky step.
When I walk away from my Mac, pause browser work safely, and when I come back, give me a one-line spoken handoff before anything continues.
Use my private accounts to answer a question, but never send the private page or raw personal data off my Mac—give me only the minimum derived result and show me exactly what was disclosed.

When I ask you to check or do something in my browser, keep it queued if the browser bridge is asleep, wake the right browser when possible, and tell me on the pendant when it is ready or why it cannot proceed—then continue automatically without me repeating myself.
Replay the last failed thing I asked for in a safe sandbox, compare it with the original pendant, relay, Mac, and browser trace, and tell me exactly which device or step diverged.

If something I asked you to do in a logged-in browser fails because the bridge is offline, tell me what failed, keep the safe read-only part, and resume it automatically when the browser reconnects—without replaying a stale form submission or click.

Keep a draft I asked you to prepare synchronized across my Mac editor and logged-in browser: if I edit it while you work, detect the conflict, preserve both versions, and tell me the smallest decision needed so I can continue without losing either one.
“The browser task failed while I was away—resume it safely and tell me exactly what ran.”
“I got interrupted—save where I am now, and when I’m back tell me exactly what to resume.”
“I was disconnected—what changed everywhere since I last heard from you?”
“If the Mac, browser, and relay disagree about whether it happened, tell me what is actually known and what I should verify.”
If an answer starts playing on my pendant and LTE drops, resume it exactly where it stopped when the link returns—without re-rendering or repeating what I already heard.
What is still pending? Give me one short status across my pendant, Mac jobs, and browser work, and tell me what will happen automatically when each connection returns.

Let the pendant notify me privately about only urgent events: use distinct vibration/light patterns for a calendar deadline, a browser account change, and a completed Mac job, and let me acknowledge or snooze each with the button without opening my phone.

Keep one task synchronized wherever I continue it: if I start dictating on the pendant, edit the draft on my Mac, and then review it in a logged-in browser tab, show me one current version and exactly what changed instead of creating duplicates or overwriting edits.
“If you start something on my Mac and the browser or connection drops, keep track of it and continue safely when it comes back—tell me what finished, what did not, and what you need from me.”
“When I’m in a focus block or meeting, keep interruptions out of my way, but collect anything important and give me one short catch-up when it ends.”
“Keep a private list of promises and follow-ups I make across email, meetings, and logged-in sites; remind me only when one is genuinely at risk, and let me close it with evidence.”
“Capture this as a decision packet, work it out while I’m away, and leave me something I can resume.”
“For the next ten minutes, let the Mac use only the shipping total and delivery date from this logged-in page; do not share anything else.”

“Park this and help me resume it later.” On a pendant tap or spoken command, save the current work context; when I say “resume the thing I parked,” restore the relevant Mac apps, browser tabs, project, and a one-sentence spoken recap without reopening secrets unnecessarily.

“Use my work account for this, but do not expose or copy my credentials.” Let me securely authorize one specific task from the pendant, have the browser use the already-open signed-in session, and receive a proof that the action used the intended account and changed only the approved fields.

If the browser is disconnected, keep my request moving: use public web access where safe, queue private-account work until Safari reconnects, and tell me exactly what is waiting instead of silently failing.

When my meeting ends, make me a private follow-up pack: collect the notes and files I touched, summarize decisions and open questions, identify promised follow-ups from my Mail and calendar context, and leave drafts/reminders for me to review—never send anything.

Keep a private commitments ledger for me: whenever I promise or accept a follow-up in a meeting, email, or logged-in web conversation, record who, what, and when; reconcile it against my Calendar, Mail, files, and browser activity; and remind me only when a commitment still lacks evidence of completion.

If I ask you to do something while my Mac or browser is offline, remember the intent, wait for the right device to reconnect, then carry it out safely and tell me exactly what happened — without losing it or doing it twice.
When the assistant fails or feels slow, tell me the actual cause and fix whatever can be fixed automatically; if it needs me, give me one clear repair step.

When I am in a meeting or deep work, quietly hold non-urgent notifications across my Mac and logged-in browser, interrupt me only for something genuinely urgent, and give me the held items as a short, ordered digest when I am free again.
“Let me have a normal conversation through the pendant even when the connection is busy—keep my speech from disappearing, and keep replies understandable.”
“Read this private page for me, but guarantee that passwords, payment details, and other secrets never leave my Mac; tell me exactly what you withheld.”
Handle this logged-in browser task even if my browser is temporarily unavailable; keep me informed and continue when it reconnects.
Answer questions using my private Mac and logged-in browser data without sending the underlying content to the cloud; tell me exactly what crossed between the Mac, browser, relay, and pendant.

When I tap twice before a meeting, put me into meeting mode: identify the next calendar event, open the right project files and browser tabs on my Mac, start a private notes workspace, mute distractions, and give me a 20-second spoken agenda; when I tap twice after, save the notes and restore what I was doing.

When I say “continue this on my Mac,” move the conversation I was having through the pendant onto the Mac exactly where I left off: show the transcript and sources, expose the unfinished plan and its next decision, attach the relevant browser tabs/files, and let me hand it back to the pendant later without starting over.
“When I’m heading into a meeting, get me ready; when I leave, turn what I captured into follow-ups.”
“Save what I’m looking at so I can pick it up later.”
“Do this when I’m no longer using the Mac, and tell me on the pendant when it’s finished.”
“I’m leaving the Mac. Save exactly where I am, and when I come back—or ask from the pendant—put me back into that work without losing anything.”
“Only let my pendant unlock or resume sensitive Mac work when I’m physically near it.”
“Verify my pendant’s 24 kHz audio path end to end, including while I’m speaking over the agent, and tell me whether it passes.”
“Let me have a genuinely natural, full-duplex 24 kHz conversation from the pendant—even when the agent is speaking—without my speech disappearing or the audio silently falling back to narrowband.”
"Continue that web task when my browser comes back, without repeating anything or losing where you got to."

entries.summary: "When I step away from my Mac, keep track of what changed and give me a private, spoken catch-up when I return—without reopening or replaying anything."
"If you tell me something important from my Mac or a logged-in website, let me ask 'why?' and hear exactly where it came from and how fresh it is."
“If you’re checking something in my logged-in browser and it goes offline, keep the task safe, tell me what paused, and resume it when the right tab comes back—without repeating steps.”
“Do this in the background without interrupting me; only speak up if it becomes urgent, otherwise leave me a complete review packet when I’m free.”

When my browser reconnects after being offline, reconcile anything queued while it was away: discard stale or duplicate commands, resume only safe read-only work, and leave me a concise pendant/Mac review showing what was skipped, resumed, or needs me.
Don’t interrupt me while I’m presenting, on a call, or actively typing; quietly queue important results, then give me a short pendant summary when I become available, with urgent exceptions only.

When I speak an instruction while the pendant has no connection, keep the useful intent locally, then finish it later when the relay and Mac are reachable—without saving the raw recording—and tell me exactly what was completed or still needs my decision.
Use my private Mac and logged-in browser data to answer questions or prepare work, but send the smallest possible redacted facts to the cloud and show me what left my devices afterward.
When I ask you to use a private browser page, recover the connection if needed, do the read-only work, and tell me clearly if the browser is unavailable instead of silently failing.

If a task on my Mac gets stuck on a choice or an expired page, ask me on the pendant, let me answer there, and resume from the exact blocked step without starting over or losing the work already done.
When a Mac or browser task is ready to send, buy, delete, or submit, read me the exact change on the pendant and let me approve or reject it there, even if I am not looking at the Mac.
“I’m focusing now.” (press pendant button) — silence routine browser/calendar noise until I press again, but interrupt me for genuinely urgent items; when focus ends, give me one short catch-up.

“Continue this on my Mac.” — hand the current pendant conversation to the Mac as a private, one-time continuation: open the relevant app or authenticated browser tab, place a concise task capsule where I can see it, and let me say “back” to return the result to the pendant.

“Let me know silently when it’s done.” — after I hand a long Mac or browser task to you, give the pendant a distinct haptic pattern for completed, needs-attention, or failed, and let a button press replay a one-sentence status.

When I ask “what am I on the hook for today?”, gather my Calendar and Mail plus the logged-in pages I have open, identify commitments, deadlines, and conflicts, and leave me a sourced review board with a short spoken summary and suggested next actions—never send, submit, or reschedule anything.

When I miss or am about to miss a commitment, tell me what is at risk, find the smallest set of recovery options across my Calendar, Mail, and logged-in work pages, and prepare a choice card on my Mac with draft messages and proposed times—then let me choose one from the pendant. Never send, submit, or reschedule without my explicit choice.
“Start meeting mode.”
“Move this conversation to my Mac.”
“Save where I am and remind me at 3—or when I get back to my Mac—then put me back exactly where I left off and give me the short version.”
“Protect my focus: interrupt me on the pendant only for something genuinely urgent; queue everything else and give me one concise catch-up when I’m free.”
“Use what I’m looking at on my Mac: read the selected text or page, answer my question about it on the pendant, and—when I say so—put the result back into the right document or browser field.”
“If one part of the system is unavailable, keep the useful part moving and tell me exactly what is waiting—then finish the private step automatically when that device comes back.”
“Play my queued briefings on the pendant, and keep going from where I left off if the connection drops.”

“When I say ‘put this in front of me,’ use the pendant to hand the conversation to my Mac: open the relevant document or logged-in page, place the exact cited passage and next action in a review note, and tell me when the handoff is ready.”
“When I walk away from my Mac, pause anything private and put my browser work into a safe state; when I come back wearing the pendant, restore only what I was actively using.”

“Make sure that actually happened everywhere I asked, and tell me if anything is out of sync.” After an action spanning my Mac and a logged-in browser, reconcile the intended end state against independent observations, identify partial completion or conflicting state, and prepare the smallest repair plan without silently retrying.

Don't interrupt me at the wrong time. Collect anything urgent from my pendant, Mac, calendar/mail, and logged-in browser, decide whether it can wait, and deliver it through the right surface when I'm actually available. If I miss it, leave one sourced, expiring queue item I can acknowledge later.

When I'm in a meeting or around other people, keep private browser, mail, and calendar details out of spoken responses. Tell me only that something needs attention, and put the details in a local Mac review panel until I explicitly unlock them.

"When a browser-dependent task is waiting, keep it safely queued and tell me on the pendant exactly whether it is queued, stale, blocked, or completed; when Chrome reconnects, resume only still-valid steps and give me one completion receipt instead of replaying old commands."

"When I'm in a meeting or presenting, keep the pendant and Mac quiet unless something is genuinely urgent; hold everything else, then give me one short catch-up when the meeting ends—without recording the meeting unless I explicitly press the button."

"For any answer or action, let me ask ‘what did you rely on?’ and hear a short source trail—what came from my Mac, browser, pendant, or the cloud, when it was observed, and what was inferred—without exposing page contents or secrets."
“Read the key number or sentence from the private page I’m looking at, say it to me once through the pendant, and forget it afterward.”
“Pause here; when I say resume, put me back exactly where I was and remind me what I was doing.”
“Why didn’t that work? Diagnose the Mac and browser connection, tell me the one thing I need to fix, and keep trying once it’s fixed.”
“Finish this when I come back, but only if nothing important changed; otherwise tell me exactly what changed before touching anything.”
When my browser extension is disconnected, still tell me what you can verify from the Mac, and queue the private-page part to finish automatically when the browser reconnects.
If I leave my Mac halfway through a task, let me resume it from the pendant later—'continue the draft' or 'finish the research'—with the exact open tabs, files, findings, and next safe step restored.

If my private browser connection breaks, tell me immediately, pause and preserve any queued work, then reconnect and resume only the safe steps without duplicating anything; give me a concise recovery report.

When I say “pause this and pick it up when I’m free,” freeze the work across my pendant, Mac, and private browser exactly where it is, save a private resume capsule, and restart it at the next suitable calendar window with a one-sentence reminder of what was waiting.

When my browser is offline, queue this request safely, do whatever can be completed on my Mac without the browser, and resume the authenticated browser steps when the bridge returns; tell me on the pendant exactly what completed, what is waiting, and what still needs my approval.

When I say “save this for later” on the pendant, capture the thought, identify what I was looking at in the browser and what meeting or project it relates to, then create one private, cited Markdown note in my AI-Pendant-Workspace and tell me where it was saved. If the browser or Mac is temporarily unavailable, hold the capsule and finish it automatically when they return.
If the pendant loses signal or I interrupt you halfway through a task, keep my place and resume it later without losing my words or repeating any Mac/browser actions.
“Make my browser available, then handle the thing I just asked about.”
“My browser was disconnected. Tell me exactly what was attempted, what never ran, and let me resume only the safe items.”

If I ask you to do something on a logged-in website while my browser is disconnected, park the request, reconnect the bridge, and continue exactly once when it is safe—then tell me what ran, what was skipped, and why. Never blindly replay the 12 commands already waiting.

When the pendant's UART or audio pipeline starts failing, file a compact bug report automatically: capture the fault window, device counters and firmware version locally, send it when the link returns, put a redacted report and reproduction hint in ~/AI-Pendant-Workspace, and tell me one short sentence—without recording microphone content.

When I say “watch this deadline” about the logged-in page I’m viewing, extract the date, obligation, and source evidence, create a local calendar reminder with a link back to that exact tab, and alert me through the pendant at a sensible lead time. If the page changes or the deadline disappears, tell me instead of silently keeping a stale reminder.

When my pendant audio sounds wrong, say “diagnose the audio path” and tell me exactly whether the fault is the pendant, relay, network, or Mac playback; save a repair-ready report without recording my microphone.

If my pendant loses the audio link during a briefing or call, keep the conversation usable: switch the output to my Mac, remember the exact playback position, and resume on the pendant when the link recovers without replaying or losing content.
“What’s going on on my computer right now, and did the thing I asked you to do actually finish?”
“If something on my Mac or logged-in browser changed while I was away, tell me whether it was me, the Pendant, or an unknown process—and let me shut down only the suspicious session.”

“If I have to leave my Mac, keep the task safe and pick it up from my pendant when I’m back: tell me what finished, what is waiting on me, and let me resume from the exact browser page or file without starting over.”
“When something important changes, tell me once on the best channel—pendant if I’m away, Mac if I’m working—and don’t repeat the same alert in my brief, dashboard, and browser.”

“Let me review something on whichever device is convenient, then approve that exact version from my pendant—even if I switch to my Mac or browser—and make every surface agree on what I approved. If anything changed, stop and show me the difference instead of guessing.”
“Save this for later” (or “make a task from what I’m looking at”).
“Show me the privacy receipt for what you just did.”

When I plug the pendant into my Mac, let me use it immediately as a private push-to-talk remote: speak through its microphone, hear the reply through its speaker, and have the Mac or my logged-in browser carry out the requested task without requiring LTE registration.

Is my pendant ready right now? Give me one honest spoken answer covering USB connection, microphone/speaker loopback, relay reachability, browser link, battery/radio state, and whether you can safely hear and act on me; if something is broken, tell me the one fix that matters first.
If I double-press the pendant, stop every AI action currently running on my Mac or in my browser, cancel queued work, and tell me through the pendant what stopped and what could not be stopped.

Use my pendant as a hardware presence key: when I physically press and hold it, authorize exactly one sensitive Mac or logged-in-browser action that is already prepared, without sending my secret or relying on a spoken confirmation.

Fill private fields in my logged-in browser using values that stay on my Mac: let the relay describe which fields are needed, have the Mac resolve the values from Keychain or an owner-approved local profile, and return only a redacted completion receipt—not the secrets.

“When my pendant is plugged into my Mac, give me a one-button ‘arrive’ routine: restore the work context I was using, tell me my next calendar commitment, and keep the spoken answer under 20 seconds.”

“When a scheduled meeting ends, make me a private wrap-up packet: the event details and attendees, relevant unread mail, the authenticated page I had open for it, three follow-up bullets, and drafts of reminders—but do not send anything.”

“If my pendant cable comes loose while you’re doing a multi-step Mac or browser task, stop at the next safe boundary, save exactly where you are, and tell me on reconnect what happened and what remains.”

From the pendant, let me ask “what do you remember about me?” and then correct or erase one fact, with a receipt showing every copy and cache that was changed.
When I press the pendant button and say “save this claim,” capture the page I’m looking at as a cited evidence card in my workspace.
While I’m watching something, let me press the pendant and say “mark the last minute,” then save a private clip marker with the video, timestamp, and my spoken note.
If I say “pause that” to the pendant while my Mac is acting, stop the current browser or Mac job, save exactly where it got to, and let me say “continue” later.
Where did I see that thing about [topic]? Search the moments I marked on the pendant, my browser pages, and my Mac notes, then tell me the best match and reopen it.
Tell me when something I saved on the pendant or in my notes conflicts with a later email, calendar change, or source page, and show me both evidence items before suggesting a correction.
"What are the four latest items on my Safari Reading List? Give me one short sentence, and open the newest one if I say 'open it'."
"Run a complete pendant audio health check now, tell me whether today's hardware is trustworthy, and file a concise bug report automatically if any acceptance number fails."
"Use the page I'm on to draft the reply, read the exact draft to me on the pendant, and send it only after I say 'send'."
"I was away for the last two hours—what changed, what needs me, and what can wait?"
"Why are you telling me that? Show me the three pieces of evidence, and tell me which part is uncertain."
"Continue this on my Mac."
“When I press the bookmark button before I walk away, save my work exactly where it is and leave me a short spoken handoff for later.”
“Turn this authenticated web page into a trustworthy brief I can keep: quote the relevant facts, show where each came from, and save it locally without sending anything or changing the site.”
“After you do that on my Mac, prove what changed and tell me if it actually worked—not just that the command ran.”
“Answer questions using my Mac, mail, calendar, files, and logged-in browser sessions, but keep the source material on the Mac—send only the minimum answer and proof back to the pendant.”
“When I make a promise out loud, remember it, watch for evidence that I completed it, and remind me only when it is genuinely at risk of being missed.”
“For anything you create or change for me, let me ask later why it exists, what I intended, and what sources or actions led to it.”
Finish the thing I’m looking at: turn the current page or document into the next concrete action, and do it.
Before anything on my Mac or in my browser sends data out, give me a one-line warning on the pendant with what would leave and where, and let me cancel it.
If a Mac or browser job gets stuck or fails while I’m away, wake me on the pendant with the reason and give me a button choice to retry safely, pause it, or leave it for later.
Give me a two-hour autonomy lease: handle routine work within the limits I say, and stop exactly when the lease expires or I revoke it from the pendant.
For a risky action, read me the exact destination and payload summary on the pendant, then let the physical button approve that one action—and prove afterward what I approved.
Lock me down now: from the pendant, close active browser sessions, pause Mac automations, revoke temporary agent authority, and show me a receipt that the lock took effect everywhere it could.
“Get me ready for my next meeting: find the meeting materials in my files and browser, build a one-page prep packet, open it beside the meeting link, and tell me the three things I need to decide.”

“Run a complete pendant bench check now, without opening the microphone: verify the USB-connected nRF9160 and audio bridge, run the synthetic two-way audio fixture, collect timing/drop counters, and leave me a pass/fail report I can attach to a bug.”

“Put me into writing mode for the next 45 minutes: identify the document I was last editing, open only the references I used for it, start the right timer, silence distracting apps, and restore my previous workspace when I say ‘I'm done’.”

“Before I act on this, check whether the calendar event, the logged-in web page, and my local documents agree. Tell me exactly which dates, names, amounts, or obligations conflict, and show me the source for each claim.”

“While I present, keep a private cue channel on the pendant: show me the current slide and my next talking point, advance the deck when I say ‘next’, capture audience questions I mark, and give me a concise question list when I finish.”

“Tell me what changed across this project since I last looked: compare local files, the relevant browser workspace, and my calendar or mail, and report only new decisions, changed deadlines, and unresolved blockers with evidence.”

When I say “protect my focus,” make my Mac, browser, and pendant enforce one interruption policy: during a calendar meeting or a focus block, suppress ordinary notifications and browser distractions, but deliver urgent messages to the pendant; when the block ends, give me one ranked catch-up list and restore what you changed.
Do the thing we just agreed on across my Mac and browser, then tell me exactly what changed and leave me a resume point if anything fails.

Every night while the pendant and audio bridge are plugged into my Mac, run a silent hardware health check; tell me in the morning only if the radio, storage, clock, or 24 kHz audio path regressed, with the exact test and last-known-good comparison.

I have 12 minutes before my next meeting—use my calendar, unread mail, and the work I already have open in the browser to choose the highest-value reversible task, do it on my Mac, and stop automatically when the time budget is up.

Before I commit to a date, deadline, or meeting in an email or browser form, check it against my calendar and existing commitments and warn me about overlaps or impossible travel time—without sending or editing anything.
Warn me through the pendant before I paste a secret, private document, or customer data into the wrong website or app, and show me exactly what kind of data was detected without repeating the secret.
“Remember this in context — the page, app, and project I’m looking at — and turn it into something I can act on later.”
“Ask me on the pendant before you send, delete, buy, or publish anything consequential, then do it and prove what happened.”
“Set up everything I need for this task, and when I’m done, put my Mac and browser back exactly as they were.”
“Undo the changes I made across my Mac and browser since 2 PM, but leave anything I changed myself alone.”
“Fill out this form using my files and calendar, but keep passwords and sensitive fields hidden from the AI, and let me review the exact submission before it goes.”
“Package everything needed to hand this project to someone else, with sources and a checklist, but strip secrets and tell me exactly what will leave my Mac.”

“Run an audio check.” The pendant should play a short private test phrase, measure the microphone-to-relay-to-Mac-to-headphones path, and tell me exactly whether the problem is capture, LTE transport, speech generation, or headphone playback—then switch to the best compatible audio profile for the next call.

“Use the best audio quality available for these headphones.” The pendant should negotiate and remember a per-headphone profile, preserving the network's 24 kHz speech quality until the final Bluetooth boundary, selecting 44.1 or 48 kHz only when required, and fall back safely when the headphones reconnect or change.
“Make the computer ready for this, then do it.”
“Use the pendant as the key for this task, and revoke it when I say stop.”

When I say “save this for later” while wearing the pendant, capture what I am looking at in Safari, the short reason I gave, and the relevant local Mac context as one private, searchable research card; keep a compact version available on the pendant when the Mac is offline, and let me later ask “why did I save this?”

If a task spans my Mac and logged-in browser, keep it alive through disconnects: retry when the right device returns, never duplicate a completed step, and tell me exactly what finished and what still needs me.

Before I rely on you, tell me whether you actually checked everything relevant across my Mac, logged-in browser, and relay-held tasks—and if you say nothing needs me, show me what was checked, what was unreachable, and how fresh each result is.

If I ask you to do something across my Mac and logged-in browser, just start it; if one part is unavailable, tell me exactly what is blocked, keep the rest moving, and resume automatically when that part comes back.

When I’m in a meeting or focused, keep the pendant silent and collect only genuinely urgent things; when I’m free, give me one short, prioritized catch-up, including anything the Mac or my logged-in browser discovered.
“Do this and keep going even if my Mac, Safari, or connection drops; tell me when it is truly finished.”

“Make sure this actually happened, not just that you clicked the button.” For example: send the prepared message, update the appointment, or change the setting, then independently verify the resulting state and tell me if reality disagrees with the intended outcome.
“If something I asked you to do fails while I’m away, keep going where it’s safe, tell me exactly what stopped, and give me one command to resume it.”
“Pack up what I’m doing so I can leave this Mac, and let me pick it up later from the pendant or another device exactly where I stopped.”

“Check that logged-in page for me. If my Mac or browser is unavailable, wait safely and finish when it comes back—tell me whether it is waiting, completed, or failed, and never repeat a step that already ran.”

“Why didn’t that work?”—give me the actual evidence from the pendant request, relay, Mac command, and browser session, explain the failure in plain language, and tell me the safest next step without rerunning anything.
“I’m leaving my Mac—save what I’m looking at and what I was trying to do, keep working on it, and give me the result on my pendant when it’s ready.”
“What am I looking at right now—and what’s the one thing I should notice?”
