entries.summary: “Run a health check on the Mac and pendant, fix anything safe, and tell me what still needs me.”
“Show me exactly how that request moved through the pendant, relay, Mac, and browser, and point to the first thing that went wrong.”
“If something I asked you to do gets stuck or fails, figure out what went wrong, try the safe alternative, and ask me on the pendant only if you truly need me.”
“Don’t just do it—make sure it actually happened, check the result from the right source, and tell me if anything disagrees.”
When I tell you to take care of something, verify that it actually stuck everywhere, and tell me exactly what is still unfinished.
If a task I handed you on my Mac fails or the connection drops, diagnose it, resume from the last completed step when safe, and tell me exactly what recovered and what still needs me.
Do it on my Mac, then prove to me that the intended result actually exists—not just that the command finished—and tell me if anything differs from what I asked for.
"If something I ask needs Safari, just do it—or tell me immediately what is offline and use another route when possible."
“Keep working, but only interrupt me if it truly matters; otherwise collect everything and tell me at a good time.”
“If the computer or browser is unavailable, figure out another safe way to finish this, or keep trying until it is available, and tell me exactly what remains.”
“Don’t just tell me you did it—verify from the actual destination that it took effect, and tell me what you checked.”

“Make sure that happened.” After any computer task, independently verify the visible result, tell me whether it really took effect, and if the Mac could not receive input, fix or retry only the uncertain part.
“Do that, and don’t tell me it worked unless you can verify the result.”
“I’m stopping here—save exactly where I am and let me resume this later from the pendant.”
“If I leave you working on my Mac or logged-in browser, let me know when it is finished or blocked—without making me check the dashboard.”
“Why is the thing I asked you to do stuck, and fix the blockage if you can?”
Run this on my Mac, keep working if it takes a while, and tell me exactly what ran, what failed, and whether you fixed it: <command or goal>.

Start this command on my Mac and stay with it. If it asks a question or needs input, tell me what it is and let me answer from the pendant; otherwise keep watching until it finishes and summarize the result.
“If the Mac work fails while I’m away, fix the harmless failures automatically and tell me exactly what ran, what failed, and what I need to do.”

“When something went wrong, show me a private, replayable movie of what every part of the pendant, relay, Mac, and browser believed happened, then let me ask ‘what if we retry just that step?’ without touching the real system.”
“Keep working on this across my Mac and logged-in browser, and tell me only when there is a real result, a decision I need to make, or something failed.”

“When something went wrong, show me one trustworthy timeline of what I said, what each part of the system observed and decided, what the Mac and browser actually changed, and the exact point where it diverged—then give me a safe way to continue from there.”
If a task gets interrupted, continue it from where it stopped and tell me what was completed, what remains, and whether anything needs my decision.
Let me start a task by voice on the pendant, pick it up on my Mac or in the browser, and hand it back to the pendant with the exact current state, evidence, and next choice preserved.
Why couldn't you do that, and what do I need to fix?

When I press the pendant and say 'save this for the project,' capture it even if my Mac or browser is unavailable, then put it in the right project when they come back—without losing it or creating duplicates.
Why can't you do that on my Mac right now—and what should I do?
Fix whatever is preventing that Mac task, or walk me through the exact fix from my pendant.
“Is my Mac ready to do that, and if not, fix whatever is stopping it?”
“I started this with the pendant—finish it on my Mac exactly where we left off, and if the browser or Mac drops out, resume safely when it returns.”
“Did that actually take effect?”

When something I asked you to do is blocked because a device, permission, or browser session is unavailable, tell me exactly what is missing, leave a recovery card on my Mac and pendant, and continue automatically when the capability returns—without repeating any irreversible step.
“Make it happen on my Mac even if the computer-use path is broken—and tell me only when it is genuinely done.”
“I’m away from my Mac—tell me what happened with the task I asked for, and if it failed, explain why and prepare the next step.”
“After you do something for me, prove that the intended real-world result actually happened, and keep checking until it does or tell me exactly what is stuck.”
Why didn't that Mac task work, and make it work if you can?

Take this multi-step task all the way through, but stop safely if any prerequisite is missing—for example, build the project on my Mac, verify the result in my authenticated browser session, then publish it and tell me exactly what happened.
Keep watch on the task I left running and tell me only if it finishes, gets stuck, or needs me.
“Reconcile this logged-in webpage with the matching files on my Mac and tell me exactly what conflicts, is missing, or is stale; prepare a clean correction plan but change nothing.”
Run this on my Mac, and if anything goes wrong, keep investigating until you can tell me exactly what happened and whether it is safe to retry.

When I say “save this for later” while I’m wearing the pendant, capture what I’m looking at on my Mac or in Safari together with my spoken note, and let me retrieve it later by asking what I saved about that topic.
When you run something on my Mac, tell me immediately if it is still running, what it produced, and if it failed, recover or explain the exact next step; I can ask the pendant 'what happened?' later.
Start this task on whichever device is available, keep going if I leave the Mac, and hand it between my pendant, browser, and Mac without losing the exact place or making me repeat anything.
“Run this terminal workflow in the background, keep me posted at meaningful milestones, and if it fails, explain the exact failing command and let me resume from there.”

“While I’m away, keep a private change ledger for my Mac, and when I ask ‘what changed?’ give me a concise, trustworthy answer with the commands, apps, and files involved—separating changes made by you from changes made by everything else.”
I’m stuck—look at what I have open, figure out the next three useful steps, and help me do the safest one.
Keep me informed without interrupting me: let only genuinely urgent things reach me as distinct silent patterns on the pendant, and give me a spoken digest when I ask.
“Make our live conversations sound wideband when the network allows, but never lose my speech just because we talk over each other.”
“Handle this logged-in browser task even if the browser is asleep—wake the Mac bridge, reconnect the browser, resume where you left off, and tell me promptly if it cannot be recovered.”

“While I was away, tell me what the system tried to do, what actually changed, what failed because a device was unavailable, and what still needs my decision—across the pendant, Mac, relay, and browser.”
When you do something on my Mac, tell me whether it actually worked; if it fails, diagnose and retry safely, and if the Mac disconnects, resume when it returns without repeating completed steps.

After I ask you to do something, let me say “show me everything that changed” and get one trustworthy timeline across my Mac, browser sessions, pendant, and relay—with the exact evidence for each side effect and a way to undo only the changes I choose.
“Do it, and make sure it actually worked.”
“I’m leaving my desk—make sure I’m not leaving anything exposed, and tell me if you couldn’t.”
When something you did on my Mac fails, tell me what happened and give me the safest concrete way to finish it.

Do this when the right moment arrives: wait until my Mac is idle, I'm not in a meeting, the right logged-in page is open, and I'm on trusted Wi‑Fi; then carry out the reversible steps and tell me what happened.
“Just do it wherever you can, and if one part of the Mac or browser is unavailable, keep going with the parts that are possible and tell me exactly what is left.”
“Watch me do this once, then let me ask you to repeat the whole workflow for me later.”
“Do it, and if one of your connections or permissions is down, recover or use another part of the hive instead of leaving me with a dead end.”
“When you say you did it, prove it—and if you can’t verify the result, tell me that instead of guessing.”
“If my Mac is asleep or disconnected, remember exactly what I asked from the pendant and finish it when the Mac comes back—without making me repeat myself.”
“Before you start, verify that the Mac and the browser session are actually reachable right now—and if one is stale, use the part that is available and tell me exactly what you could not verify.”

“Keep working on this across my Mac and logged-in browser even if I walk away or one device disconnects; resume from the last safe checkpoint and tell me exactly what finished, what failed, and what I should do next.”

“Pause what I’m doing here and give me this exact work state back later, wherever I am.” The pendant should snapshot my active Mac window, browser tabs and selections, unsaved text, relevant terminal state, and the spoken reason; later I can say “resume the paused thread” and have the Mac and authenticated browser restore the right state before the pendant reminds me where I left off.

“While I’m concentrating, decide which things are worth interrupting me for across my Mac and logged-in browser, and hold everything else until I’m free.” The pendant should let me change the mode with one button press or a short phrase, announce only genuinely urgent items, and give me a compact deferred queue when I switch modes.
“If something can’t run on my Mac, tell me exactly why, fix what can be fixed, and give me the best fallback instead of just failing.”
“Put what I just said into the thing I’m looking at.”
“Do that on my Mac, and if anything fails or the Mac disconnects, keep the work safe, resume from the last confirmed step, and tell me exactly what ran and what remains.”
“Whenever you tell me something important, let me ask ‘show me why’ and take me straight to the exact source on my Mac or in the browser—without making me repeat the question.”
“Before you start, tell me whether the Mac, browser, relay, and pendant can actually do this—and if one is unavailable, keep going with the best safe route and tell me exactly what I need to fix.”
“Show me exactly what happened across the pendant, relay, Mac, and browser when my request went wrong—and tell me the one thing I should do next.”

“If I tell you something while the network or Mac is unavailable, remember it on the pendant, acknowledge that it is safely queued, and carry it out or ask me about it when the connection returns—without losing or duplicating it.”
“Keep an eye on my Mac and browser bridge. If a job is stuck or the bridge goes offline, tell me on the pendant, retry safe work when it comes back, and give me one concise recovery report.”

“When I’m away from my Mac, let me tap the pendant to queue a task with a short voice note; when I get back, have the relay and Mac resume it from the right project and tell me exactly what completed, without making me repeat myself.”
“Read this private log or folder and tell me what matters, but do not send the raw contents off my Mac.”
“If one of my devices is unavailable, keep the request alive and finish it through the best available path—and tell me plainly what is waiting, what already happened, and what could not be done.”
“Remember this exactly where I found it, and let me ask about it later from the pendant even if that tab or my Mac is closed.”
“Only show private Mac and logged-in-browser results when I’m actually wearing the pendant; if I take it off, pause the sensitive work and continue when I put it back on.”
“For that request I made earlier, show me the complete chain of what happened, what is still queued, what failed, which device did each step, and roughly how much model time it cost.”

“After anything gets interrupted, tell me what is definitely complete, what is only partly done, and what cannot be verified—and offer the next safest way to reconcile it without blindly repeating the action.”
If something I asked you to do fails while I'm away, figure out why, try the safest equivalent route on the Mac or in my logged-in browser, and tell me only what worked and what still needs me.
“Tell me which parts of my AI assistant were slow or unreliable today, what they cost, and automatically improve the routing for tomorrow without changing what actions it is allowed to take.”
“When something fails, tell me in one sentence what stopped it, show me the evidence if I ask, and tell me the fastest safe way to continue—without making me repeat the whole request.”

“Did that actually happen?” — give me one trustworthy answer about a multi-step task, including what the Mac did, what Safari changed, whether the relay delivered it, and what remains uncertain after an interruption.
“That failed—figure out what went wrong, pick up from the last successful step, and finish it.”
“Pack up what you’re doing so I can close the lid, then continue it later exactly where you left off.”
“The thing I asked you to do on my Mac failed—figure out why, try the safest repair, and tell me exactly what you changed.”
“While you’re working on my Mac, let me know from the pendant—without opening a conversation—when it finishes, gets stuck, or needs me.”
“Keep this terminal task alive while I leave, and when I come back let me continue it from exactly where it stopped—without starting over.”

When something I asked takes multiple steps, show me one trustworthy timeline of what the pendant heard, what the relay decided, what the Mac or browser actually did, and what remains undone — with a one-tap way to retry only the failed step.

While I’m focused, quietly decide whether a new Mac or browser notification is worth interrupting me: use what app or page it came from, my current calendar context, and urgency; tell me immediately on the pendant only when it truly matters, and leave everything else in a review queue.
“Continue the thing that failed when my browser was offline.”
“Why did that take so long, and what exactly happened on my Mac?”
“Make the Mac ready so you can use my browser and see the screen.”

When I ask you to do something in Safari, start immediately; if the browser bridge is offline, tell me right away and continue automatically when it reconnects, then give me one completion or failure report instead of making me ask again.

When you run something on my Mac and it fails, diagnose it locally, try a safe alternative way to accomplish the same goal, and tell me exactly what worked, what did not, and what changed—without making me repeat the request.

Take the file I mention on my Mac, verify that it is the right version, upload it to the matching form in my logged-in browser, and show me the exact file, destination, and fields before anything is submitted.
“If something can’t run right now, don’t leave me waiting—tell me what is unavailable, use the best safe fallback, and keep the original task ready to resume when the device comes back.”
“If I lose connection while you’re doing something, pick up the same conversation where we left off—without making me repeat myself or doing an action twice.”
"Keep my browser tasks reliable: if Safari disconnects, stop retrying blindly, tell me once what is waiting, resume when it reconnects, and never alert me about the same page change twice."
"When you change something for me, don't just say the command ran—check that the intended result is actually true, keep watching it briefly, and tell me if it failed or was undone."

When the pendant notices a crash or I say “file this bug,” collect the relevant UART/device log, reproduce context, and leave a ready-to-review issue draft on my Mac with a short spoken summary—never submit it automatically.
When I double-press the pendant while I’m listening, bookmark the exact moment and later give me a searchable note with the surrounding transcript, audio clip, and any related Mac or browser context.

When I ask you to do something involving my browser, just proceed: use the fastest available route, automatically fall back for public pages when Safari is offline, queue private-page work until the bridge returns, and tell me on the pendant exactly what ran, what was deferred, and why.

When several background tasks finish or fail while I am away, give me one interruption at the right moment that bundles only the decisions I need, lets me ask for any receipt, and otherwise leaves everything quietly queued.
“Keep my browser work reliable: if Safari or the bridge drops, preserve my queued requests, tell me what is stuck, and when it comes back reconcile each request and continue only the safe ones.”
“I’m leaving my Mac. Package up exactly where I am across my open tabs and apps, and when I’m back, bring me back to the right place and remind me what I was doing.”
“Give me a focused 25-minute block. Keep my Mac and browser quiet, but let through anything genuinely urgent, and tell me when the block is over.”

When something I asked you to do on my Mac or in Safari fails, recover it automatically when it is safe, switch to the other available surface when possible, and tell me exactly what happened without making me repeat the request.
If my Mac or Safari is unavailable when I ask, remember the exact task on the pendant, tell me it is queued, and resume it automatically when the right surface comes back—without me asking again.

Just do it, but first figure out which parts of my Mac, browser, pendant, and relay are actually available; use safe fallbacks when one is unavailable, and tell me what you could not do without making me ask again.
After you do something across my Mac and logged-in browser, tell me whether it actually took effect—not merely whether the commands succeeded—and show me the short before/after proof if I ask.
“If my Mac or browser connection is unhealthy, keep my request moving where it can, tell me what could not run, and retry the missing Mac steps when it recovers.”
“When something failed, tell me whether it is safe to retry, what already happened, and retry only the missing pieces.”
“Save what I’m looking at right now for me, with enough evidence that I can trust it later, and let me pick it back up from the pendant without reopening the page.”
"Keep trying that browser task, and tell me on the pendant when it actually succeeds."
"Make this Mac ready for you to control, and tell me exactly what I still need to click."
Make my Mac ready for AI control, and tell me the one thing I need to fix.
Restore my work exactly where I left off after my Mac or browser restarts.
“Compare the information in this private browser page with my local files, tell me what conflicts, and prepare a local report I can review—without sending the private contents to the cloud.”
From the pendant, “run that build/test and tell me only when it finishes or needs me,” even if I walk away or the Mac briefly loses its connection.

“Did that actually happen?” — give me one trustworthy answer about a task that crossed my Mac, logged-in browser, and pendant, showing what changed, what did not, and the evidence for each step without running it again.
Fix the thing that just failed on my Mac.
When something breaks, file a complete bug report for me automatically.
“If you can’t control my Mac, fix the connection with me and tell me when it is genuinely ready.”
“If my Mac loses control or goes offline, keep the task alive and let me finish it from the pendant without starting over.”
If something I asked you to do on my Mac fails or gets stuck, diagnose it, try the safest available alternate route, and tell me exactly what happened without making me ask again.

When I ask “what did you do for that?”, show me one trustworthy, chronological answer covering the pendant, relay, Mac shell, and browser: what was attempted, what actually changed, what failed, and the evidence—without rerunning anything.

When I say “stop that” to the pendant, cancel every still-running part of that request across the relay, Mac, and browser, leave completed changes untouched, and tell me exactly what was stopped and what could not be stopped.

“If something I asked you to do fails while I’m away, figure out whether it can be safely retried, retry it when the Mac or browser comes back, and tell me exactly what succeeded, what was skipped, and why.”

“After I approve a form, booking, or message from my pendant, submit it in my logged-in browser and prove that the service accepted exactly what I approved; if the result is ambiguous, stop and tell me instead of submitting twice.”
“If you lose connection while doing that, keep the work safe: resume only while my request is still fresh, and tell me exactly whether it finished, was abandoned, or needs me.”
“Make the computer-control connection usable again, and stay with me until you know it really works.”
Make computer control work again, and tell me exactly what I need to fix.
“If something you delegated fails, recover it without making me repeat myself, and tell me only when you need my help.”
“Why did you do that, and what would have happened if you had chosen differently?”
“Do that, and tell me whether it really happened.”
“Set this up and keep making sure it stays that way.”
If something I asked the Mac or browser to do failed—or may have silently done nothing—figure out why, recover with the safest working route, and tell me exactly what happened.
Pause this wherever it is, keep the exact place and evidence, and resume it when I’m back at my Mac—tell me only what changed while I was away.
If something I asked you to do fails while I’m away, figure out why, retry safely when possible, and tell me exactly what happened when I’m back.
When my Mac or browser comes back online, tell me what was waiting, what expired, and what you resumed—then let me say 'resume the safe ones' or 'drop them' from the pendant.

When I’m trying to focus, quietly watch what is happening across my Mac and logged-in browser, and tell me only when something genuinely time-critical changes—otherwise hold everything until I’m free.

When I leave my Mac in the middle of something, remember exactly where I stopped; when I come back, give me a short spoken 'resume here' briefing and offer to restore the relevant tabs, app, and draft without losing unsaved work.

When I press the pendant button and say “save this moment,” save my words together with what is currently on my Mac screen and in my active browser tab, then later let me ask “what was that thing I saved?” and jump back to the exact evidence and context.
When something fails on my Mac, tell me exactly what ran, what it could reach, why it failed, and what you recommend next — in one short spoken explanation.

Make this true everywhere: after I ask you to change something, keep checking the Mac and my logged-in browser until the requested end state is verified, then tell me whether it is actually done—not merely whether an action ran.
If my Mac and a logged-in website disagree about whether something is finished, warn me and show both pieces of evidence before doing anything else.

When I tell you to do something on my computer, use whatever route can actually reach it, and tell me plainly if it was completed, partially done, or impossible—never say success when the Mac or browser could not receive the action.
Make computer control work again, and walk me through whatever my Mac needs—then verify it actually works before trying the task again.

If something I asked you to do in Safari gets stuck, recover it automatically when possible; otherwise tell me in one short pendant message what is blocked, what you tried, and whether anything changed.

When Safari says an action timed out, tell me whether it actually took effect anyway—without repeating it—and keep checking until you can prove the final state or tell me exactly what remains unknown.

When I ask you to do something on my Mac, tell me truthfully whether it actually happened—and if the Mac or browser cannot reach the screen, recover through another path or leave a clearly tracked pending job instead of claiming success.

If I start a task on my pendant and then walk away or lose the connection, have the system resume it on the right Mac/browser session later, remember exactly what I meant, and tell me what changed since I last heard from it—without making me repeat the request.

“Why did you do that, and what exactly happened?” Give me a trustworthy, chronological explanation of everything the pendant, relay, Mac, and browser saw, decided, attempted, changed, and failed to do for one request, with links or spoken evidence for each step and a clear list of uncertainties.
When my browser is offline, queue only the browser work I explicitly asked for, and when it reconnects tell me what was skipped, what ran, and why—never replay stale commands blindly.
My Mac actions stopped taking effect—walk me through fixing the AI Pendant Agent permission, open the right setting, and verify that typing/clicking really works before you continue.

When I ask the pendant to do something on my Mac or in my browser, make sure the intended real-world result happened—not merely that a command returned—and tell me the evidence or the exact point where verification failed.
Make this happen on my Mac, and don't tell me it worked unless it really did—even if the usual UI controls are unavailable.
Before my next meeting, check whether I can realistically make it, open the route on my Mac, and if I'm going to be late prepare a message for me—but don't send anything unless I say so.

If my Mac or browser is unavailable, still answer what you can: use public web sources as a fallback, clearly say when a private logged-in source could not be reached, and resume the private task automatically when the connection returns.

When my Mac, logged-in browser, and relay have conflicting facts about the same task, tell me exactly what disagrees and ask one small clarifying question before acting. Keep both pieces of evidence attached so I can say which one is right and continue without starting over.
Why didn't that work?
Find the current, canonical version of this thing across my Mac and logged-in browser, and tell me what conflicts.
“Just do it on whichever device can actually reach it, and if something is offline or unavailable, tell me immediately and continue with the parts that still work.”
“If my Mac, browser, or internet drops halfway through, remember exactly where you were and finish safely when the right device comes back—without repeating anything or making me start over.”
If my Mac or browser is offline, keep my request pending, and when it reconnects carry out only the safe, repeatable parts, then tell me from the pendant exactly what ran, what was skipped, and why.

When I step away from my Mac during an AI task, keep my place privately and make the work safe to resume; when I return, let me continue from the pendant or Mac without reopening sensitive pages or losing the in-progress state.

“Did that actually happen?” — verify the real-world result across my Mac and logged-in browser, not just whether an agent returned success, and tell me what is confirmed, what is only prepared, and what could not be checked.
“I’m offline right now—remember this exactly and carry it out when the right device comes back, but tell me if anything changed before you do it.”

“Make this safe to share.” Use what I’m currently viewing in Safari and the relevant local Mac files to create a redacted share packet, save it locally, and stage it in the right browser upload or message composer without sending anything.

“Take care of this whole task, even if I walk away or the browser/Mac connection drops. Resume where you left off, and when you’re done tell me exactly what changed, what could not be completed, and show me the evidence.”

“I got interrupted—what was I doing, what is still unfinished, and put me back where I left off.” The pendant should give me a short spoken reconstruction and, if I say ‘restore it,’ reopen the relevant Mac windows and reattach the browser tabs without submitting or sending anything.

“What private information did you use for that, and what left my Mac?” Give me a plain-language data-flow receipt for the last request, including which browser pages, files, apps, model tier, and relay paths were involved.
From the pendant, run the task across my Mac and browser, then tell me whether it really completed; if a transient bridge or command failure occurs, retry safely and show me the exact failed step.

When I tell the pendant “handle this when my computer is available,” save the intent, then later continue across my Mac and authenticated browser—even if both are offline now—and tell me what changed, what was skipped, and why.

Keep my Mac and authenticated browser in sync after a multi-step request—for example, if you book something in the browser and add it to Calendar—then detect partial completion, repair the missing side, and tell me exactly which sides succeeded.

“When you submit something in my authenticated browser, make sure the Mac records it only after the site confirms it, and tell me later exactly what happened—even if the browser or Mac disconnects halfway through.”
Make the AI Pendant Browser Bridge available, wait for a fresh heartbeat, and tell me in one short sentence whether it is online—without replaying or executing any queued browser command.

If I speak while the Mac or relay is temporarily offline, keep my request on the pendant, show me that it is queued, and deliver it exactly once when the connection returns—then tell me whether it was accepted, completed, or needs me.
“Open the page I mentioned, keep trying if my Mac or Safari bridge briefly drops, and tell me only when you have verified the exact page is open—or give me the precise reason it cannot be reached.”
If something I asked the pendant to do fails, recover it automatically when it is safe, otherwise tell me exactly what broke, what was tried, and what I need to do.

Before you use my Mac or logged-in browser, tell me exactly what information will leave the device, what will stay local, and which model or service will see each piece; let me choose a private-local mode when possible.
“That didn’t work—tell me exactly why, try the safest recovery, and leave me a reviewable fallback if it still fails.”
“Pause this exactly where it is, remember what I was looking at and what remains, and resume it when I’m back at my Mac—without losing the browser context.”
“If something truly urgent happens, reach me on the pendant; otherwise wait until I’m free and put it on the Mac. Escalate only if I haven’t acknowledged it.”
When I say “save this page” through the pendant, remember the exact Safari page and the part I’m looking at, then let me ask for it back later.

During a meeting, let me tap the pendant once to bookmark what is happening; afterward give me a timeline of my bookmarks with the active meeting, the Safari page on screen, and a short note for each.

If the pendant stops responding, let me ask “what’s wrong?” and have the Mac inspect both USB devices, the relay pipeline, and the last audio/job receipts, then tell me the cause and recover what can be recovered.

When I walk away from my Mac, quietly checkpoint whatever I was doing, and when I return with the pendant, restore the right Safari tabs, window layout, and unfinished draft without sending or submitting anything.

Let the pendant act as my interruption filter: during a focus block, collect notifications from my Mac and authenticated browser, interrupt me only for things that meet my urgency rule, and give me a one-button way to defer the rest until I am free.

When I say “hand this off,” package the exact current browser or Mac state into a private, expiring handoff that another device or a later session can reopen at the same point, with my unsent draft and source citations intact.

Keep my pendant conversational when it is plugged into my Mac, even if LTE or the relay is unavailable: I press the button, speak, hear the response through the audio bridge, and sync the transcript and pending work when connectivity returns.

Give me a private-mode answer: inspect my currently open authenticated Safari tabs and local Mac state, but keep the page contents and audio on my Mac; send the relay only a redacted request and a short answer, with a switch to reveal the evidence if I ask.

When I say 'continue that later' on the pendant, save the exact state of the conversation and the open Mac/browser work, then let me resume from the pendant or Mac with a one-sentence spoken checkpoint and no repeated explanation.

If the Mac or browser agent starts doing something I no longer want, let me long-press the pendant to stop all in-flight work immediately, hear what was cancelled, and later resume only the safe unfinished parts.

Make my Mac and browser automatically enter a private state when my pendant leaves me: pause spoken output, hide sensitive Safari tabs, stop sharing, and restore everything when the pendant returns—without me touching the keyboard.

When a sensitive value is visible in my authenticated browser—such as a one-time code, delivery address, or account number—let me ask from the pendant for just that value and whisper it locally through the audio bridge, without sending the page or value through the relay.
“The task failed—figure out why, repair what you can, retry only the failed part, and tell me if it is truly finished.”
“Use the pendant over USB as my physical job remote: start the queued Mac/browser task, show progress with its light or haptic feedback, and alert me only when it needs a decision.”
“What did you change on my Mac and in my browser since [time]?”
“Tap my pendant to bind this exact Safari tab and the app I’m looking at, then let me ask about or act on that context without telling you which tab it is.”
“Don’t just tell me this is done—prove it from the actual file, app, or webpage, and show me the evidence if it isn’t.”
“Pack up exactly where I am—open tabs, relevant files, unsent drafts, and the next safe step—so I can resume this work later with one tap.”
“Something in my project just failed—find the cause, fix the safe parts, and tell me exactly what changed.”
“Even when the relay is down, let me press the pendant button and hear a local status or saved instruction through my headphones; sync what happened when the Mac reconnects.”
“Make the pendant agent able to control the screen again, and prove it worked.”
“Read the authenticated page I’m looking at into my headphones, skip the boilerplate, and let the pendant pause, resume, or jump to the next section.”
“Test the pendant and headphones end to end, and tell me what is actually broken.”
“If something you ran fails, fix it yourself and tell me exactly what changed.”
“When I unplug the pendant, save exactly where we are; when I plug it back in, pick up from there and tell me what happened while I was away.”
“If I tap the pendant twice, stop starting new work everywhere, finish nothing silently, and tell me what is still running when I’m ready.”
“When the pendant is plugged into my Mac, keep the whole assistant working even if the relay or LTE is down.”

“Before you change anything across my Mac and logged-in browser, show me a machine-checkable forecast of every file, tab, account field, and device state that will change—and after you do it, prove the forecast matched reality.”
“Use my saved credentials and one-time codes to complete this login, but never reveal the secrets to you, the relay, the browser page text, or the action history.”
“Hand this task to Alex for the next hour, but give them only the exact browser tab and files needed, and revoke everything automatically afterward.”
“Mark this moment.”
“Fix that failure and tell me what you changed.”
“Read the useful parts of this download to me.”
“Stop everything you’re doing.”
“What did I decide about this, and what evidence led me there?”
“Make this private now.”
“Tell me when my sources disagree about something important.”
“Press the pendant button and read me what I’m looking at.”

entries.summary: “When I’m offline, let me tap the pendant to run my usual Mac shortcuts and tell me whether each one worked.”
“When I walk away from my Mac, protect my private browser tabs automatically, and restore them when I come back with the pendant.”
“Watch me do this once, then let me repeat the routine from the pendant without asking me to explain every step.”
“If something I asked you to do fails, fix it yourself using the best available surface and tell me exactly what you recovered.”
“What time is it?” and “When will my scheduled brief actually run?” should always use my real timezone, even when the Mac, relay, and pendant disagree.
“Use the clearest voice you can, and if the audio link degrades, keep talking and catch me up when it recovers.”
“When I’m in a meeting or around other people, keep private information out of the room, but still let me know if something truly urgent needs me.”
“Before you say anything sensitive out loud or use my logged-in accounts, make sure I’m actually the person wearing the pendant.”
“Don’t interrupt me three times about the same thing; give me one alert at the best moment and remember that I’ve acknowledged it everywhere.”
“I’m busy—queue this. When I next press the pendant button, read me the most important completed result, and let me say ‘open it’ to continue on the Mac or in the exact logged-in browser tab.”

“I’m stepping away.” Lock down my active Mac and logged-in browser work, pause anything speaking aloud, and when I press the pendant again restore only the tabs and jobs I was using—not unrelated sessions.

“Start meeting mode.” Use the pendant as the control and audio endpoint, identify the meeting I’m currently in from my Mac and calendar/browser context, privately transcribe it while it runs, and when I end it give me only decisions, owners, and deadlines—with drafts saved but nothing sent.

“Use my private identity for this form.” Fill only the requested identity fields from my encrypted vault, show me the exact field mapping, and require a deliberate pendant button gesture before the browser receives any secret; never speak or place the secret in model context.

“Review what I changed.” Read the active project and git diff on my Mac, inspect related authenticated issue or documentation tabs if needed, explain the three riskiest changes through the pendant, and let me approve a precise patch plus tests without ever silently committing or pushing.
“What am I looking at?” — answer from the screen and the active Safari page, then let me ask a follow-up by voice.
“Compare this page with my local notes/project and tell me what conflicts.”
“If something you’re doing fails while I’m away, diagnose it and tell me the next useful step when I’m back.”
“Explain the thing I just copied.”
“Test the whole pendant setup.”
“Use my pendant over USB right now, even though it has no LTE.”
“Review what I’m about to commit and tell me the one thing most likely to hurt me.”
“If my Mac or browser gets stuck while I’m away, recover it and tell me only if I need to intervene.”
“Press the pendant button to start a work session, do the task on my Mac and in Safari, then press it again to give me a reproducible timeline and a resume point if anything failed.”

“If I lose the USB connection while you’re working, keep the unfinished Mac task queued on the pendant and finish it automatically when I plug back in; tell me exactly what was completed and what was skipped.”

“When something breaks, press the pendant and say ‘make a bug report’: capture the current Mac app, screen, relevant logs and browser page, turn them into a concise reproducible report, and open a draft in my issue tracker without submitting it.”

“Test the pendant and audio bridge”: build or flash the current firmware, run a scripted USB serial hardware check, press/observe the button and LED, exercise bridge audio loopback, and give me a pass/fail report with the failing component and logs.

“If I long-press the pendant, immediately stop every Mac task this system started, close the private browser tabs it opened, and put the whole hive into a paused state; tell me what was actually stopped when I release.”

“Find duplicate downloads and project files across my Mac and Safari, group them by content rather than filename, and leave a reviewable cleanup plan with safe quarantine actions—do not delete anything.”

“While I’m away from the Mac, turn important Mac and browser events into a small tactile queue on the pendant: blink patterns identify the source, a button press marks one read, and when I reconnect, give me the exact underlying event—not just a generic notification.”
“Start this from my pendant and keep it alive across the Mac, Safari, and relay—even if I walk away or the USB link drops; tell me only when it needs me or is truly finished.”
“If something you ran on my Mac fails, figure out the cause, try the safest alternative automatically, and tell me in plain language what changed—don't make me repeat the whole task.”
“I may have several things running. Decide which result deserves to interrupt me on the pendant, bundle the rest into one later digest, and let me ask ‘what did I miss?’ to hear the exact outcomes.”

“When you act on my behalf, let me ask ‘why did you do that?’ and hear a compact, evidence-linked explanation of what I said, what each node observed, which alternatives you rejected, and exactly what changed.”
“I’m leaving—keep an eye on the task, recover from transient Mac or browser failures yourself, and tell me on the pendant only when it is truly done or needs me.”

“That CI-failure email is important—trace it all the way through: open the authenticated notification, inspect the matching repository and workflow on my Mac, run only diagnostic checks, correlate the evidence, and leave me a cited spoken incident report with the next command I should approve.”
“If I press and hold the pendant button, stop the currently running Mac or browser task immediately, tell me which step was halted, and leave a resumable checkpoint for later.”
“Why is my computer slow right now? Check the Mac, open browser tabs, network, disk, and the pendant audio link together, identify the actual bottleneck, and fix only a reversible cause.”

“Make this reproducible.” Capture the exact pendant request, model/routing decision, browser tabs and URLs, Mac cwd and environment fingerprint, commands, outputs, and timing into a private replay bundle I can inspect or hand to you later.

“Before I send this, check every attachment, quoted passage, browser field, and local file for secrets or private data, explain the risks in plain language, and prepare a clean redacted version without sending anything.”
“I’m stuck—look at what I’m doing and tell me the next step.”
“Quiet mode for the next hour.”
“I just left that meeting—what did I promise, and put the follow-ups where I’ll see them?”
“Read the thing I’m looking at, privately, and tell me what it means.”
“Warn me only when something I’ve committed to is about to collide with something else.”
“Handle this, but keep anything private on my Mac and tell me exactly what leaves it.”
“Start this job on my Mac and keep me informed through the pendant—even if I walk away or the internet drops.”
“Before I submit this form or send this message, tell me exactly what information is about to leave my Mac, where it is going, and what I copied from my private tabs.”
“Only interrupt me when something is genuinely urgent: combine my Mac notifications, calendar context, and logged-in browser changes, then explain why you interrupted me on the pendant.”

“When I have a thought while I’m away from my Mac, let me capture it immediately on the pendant, keep it safe offline, and turn it into the right reminder, project note, or follow-up when I’m next connected.”

“When I say ‘save that’ or ‘send that to my Mac,’ use what I was just hearing plus the page or selection currently in front of me, and put the right excerpt in the right note—without making me repeat it.”
“Know when I’ve left my Mac and stop reading private things aloud; queue the useful result, then resume it safely when I’m wearing the pendant nearby again.”
“This CI failure email looks bad—investigate it and prepare the smallest fix, but don’t push or send anything.”
“Before I run this command, tell me what it is likely to change or break.”
“I’m holding the pendant—capture a health report for this Mac and the pendant/bridge, and tell me if anything is actually disconnected.”
“What changed on my Mac and in my open browser sessions since yesterday that might matter to me?”
“Did anything I just ran expose a secret or personal data outside this Mac?”
“What did you and the other surfaces actually do for me today, and what changed in the outside world?”
“Make the pendant audio work reliably, and keep it sounding as clear as the connection allows.”
“Run an end-to-end pendant audio test now, tell me exactly where quality or latency fails, and leave the fixes ready to apply.”
“If I walk away from the Mac or lose LTE, keep my conversation alive and continue it when the pendant reconnects.”
“When I say ‘save this moment,’ put the useful context around what I’m looking at and hearing into one private note I can find later.”
“While I’m wearing and holding the pendant, let it act as the key to a private working session across my Mac and browser; when I release it, stop sharing that context everywhere.”
When something I asked you to do fails or seems not to happen, tell me exactly where it stopped—pendant, relay, Mac, browser, or external site—show the evidence and retry only the failed stage.
Use the button on my pendant to confirm or cancel the exact Mac or browser action you just prepared, even when the pendant is only USB-connected to my Mac and the relay has not registered it.

For any answer or action involving my Mac, browser, pendant, or relay, tell me in one glance which surfaces and data were actually used, what stayed local, what left the Mac, and how fresh each fact was.
When the Mac, browser, and relay disagree about what is true, show me the conflicting evidence and ask exactly one useful question instead of silently choosing a version.

Let me demonstrate a repetitive task once on my Mac or in Safari, then have you turn it into a reusable routine with the changing fields identified, a preview of the next run, and a spoken way to invoke it from the pendant.
“Save this research trail so I can pick it up tomorrow—even if the browser tabs change.”
“I’m about to unplug the Mac—keep listening for short notes and quietly file them, then bring me a concise catch-up when I reconnect.”
“I’m going into a meeting—make the computer quiet, keep anything urgent for me, and catch me up when I press the pendant afterward.”
“When the pendant or bridge misbehaves, file a complete bug report for me.”
“That CI failure email is urgent—find the failing code, explain it, and prepare the smallest fix for review.”
“If Safari cannot read a page, recover automatically and tell me what actually happened.”
“What happened across my pendant, browser, and Mac while I was away? Give me one trustworthy timeline.”
“Save the report I’m viewing in Safari into my workspace, verify it, and tell me exactly where it landed.”
“When the pendant notices I’m back at my Mac, restore the work context I left there and tell me what needs attention.”

When I press the pendant while it is USB-connected, let me say or choose a command for my Mac, execute it locally even with no LTE, and hear a truthful result; if I unplug it, queue the same request and finish it when the relay returns.

Calibrate my wearable audio link: play a deterministic sweep through the nRF9160 and ESP32 bridge, measure USB/I2S/Bluetooth timing and dropouts, then save the correction profile and tell me whether the link is healthy.
That Mac command failed — diagnose the actual exit condition, show me the smallest repair, and retry only the failed step without repeating anything that already succeeded.
Send this reply privately to my headphones, or play it on the Mac speakers instead, and remember the choice for this conversation.
Keep working on this even if my Mac goes to sleep: wake it when needed, continue the local/browser steps, and tell me on the pendant whether it finished, is waiting for the Mac, or failed.
“Stop whatever you just started, even if the Mac is still in the middle of a shell command, and tell me exactly what was stopped and what I can safely resume.”
“What needs me right now? Combine anything waiting in my authenticated browser tabs with failed or paused Mac work, rank it by consequence, and let me resolve each item by voice.”

“Turn the thing I’m looking at in the browser into a ready-to-review change in my active project: extract the relevant requirements, edit the right files on the Mac, run the tests, and tell me what changed.”

“I’m leaving my desk—put everything into away mode: pause resumable Mac work, freeze authenticated browser sessions without logging me out, save exactly where each task was, and tell me on the pendant what will resume when I return.”

“Finish this overnight, but only while my Mac is plugged in and idle; use the authenticated browser session if needed, stop before my morning routine, and leave me a spoken result or the exact blocker.”
“What changed on my Mac while I was away, and is anything waiting for me?”
“Run the long task now, keep working if I close the lid, and tell me only when it reaches a real milestone or needs me.”
“Tell me why the project stopped being green, and open the exact files and issue pages I need to fix it.”
“Read me the important parts of this private page, but never say sensitive details aloud if my headphones are not actually connected.”
When I say “don’t interrupt me unless it matters,” have the pendant and Mac decide what deserves an interruption, and give me one concise catch-up when I become available.
When a Mac or browser task fails, press the pendant button once and say “fix that”; have the system capture what failed, repair it, and tell me exactly what changed or why it stopped.
While I work, notice a repeated sequence I perform across Safari and Mac apps, and later ask me once whether to turn that exact sequence into a spoken command I can run from the pendant.
Do this across my Mac and browser, and do not tell me it succeeded until you can verify the result I asked for; if verification fails, keep working or explain the exact blocker.

Keep working on this for me even when my Mac sleeps: monitor the authenticated browser page or Mac task I named, wake or reconnect when necessary, and tell me through the pendant only when the specific condition I described becomes true.
When I walk away with the pendant, hide sensitive browser and Mac content, and restore it when I return; if the pendant link is uncertain, leave the screen protected and tell me why.
Watch this authenticated checkout or booking page and complete it only if the final terms stay within the limits I said; otherwise keep the reservation or draft ready and ask me through the pendant.
“Run that Mac command, and if it fails, figure out why and recover without asking me.”
“What exactly did you do on my Mac and in Safari while I was away? Give me one replayable report, not a vague summary.”
“Keep this whole task alive while I move between my Mac, Safari, and the pendant; if any link drops, resume from the last verified step and tell me only what still needs me.”
“Undo everything that task changed, across my Mac and Safari, and leave anything you couldn’t safely undo untouched.”
“Before you act, prove you’re in the right account and workspace; if Mac and Safari disagree, stop and tell me exactly which identity is wrong.”
“Make my voice audio HD for this call.” Then keep the 24 kHz wideband path end to end and tell me if any link falls back.
“What exactly failed on the Mac?” after a command or browser action, and give me one short spoken diagnosis with a retry option.
“Run this when my Mac is idle and on power, then tell me what it found.”
“Put this one-time code into the login page, but never repeat or save it.”
“Privacy stop.” Then immediately mute the pendant, stop sending audio, pause agent work, and lock down my active browser session until I resume it.
“Keep my AI costs under $25 this month without me micromanaging it.”
“Turn what I just did into a button I can press next time.”
“That failed while I was away — tell me why, and retry it safely if the world is still the same.”
“Package this task so another agent can finish it tomorrow without asking me the same questions.”
“Remember that correction and apply it automatically next time, but show me what you learned.”
“Before you tell me this is done, prove it with the smallest evidence packet I can inspect.”

When I press the pendant and ask “what am I looking at?”, read the active Safari tab I’m actually viewing, summarize only the useful content aloud, and if the page is inaccessible tell me exactly why instead of retrying blindly.

Every weekday morning, inspect the authenticated tabs I have already left open, group only items that need my attention today, and read me a five-item maximum digest with the tab name and a direct next action.

Let me say “I need to finish this before I leave” on the pendant, then have the system watch the active Mac project and authenticated browser tabs, detect the smallest concrete next step, and remind me only when that step is actually unblocked—silently deferring reminders while I am speaking or presenting.

When I say “I’m going into a meeting,” have the pendant and Mac create a temporary focus contract: suppress noncritical voice and browser notifications, capture urgent items into a private queue, and give me one prioritized spoken handoff when I say “I’m back.”

If the relay or internet drops while I am wearing the pendant, let me keep asking short commands and get spoken answers from my Mac over the live USB pendant and audio bridge, then reconcile the conversation with the relay when it returns without repeating actions.
"What's running on my Mac right now, what is stuck, and if I say stop that one, stop exactly that one?"
"Let me talk to you through the pendant over the Mac's USB connection even when LTE has never registered."
"Run the test/build and tell me whether it actually passed; if it fails, give me the first useful error and leave me a report I can reopen."
"I’m screen-sharing now—make the whole hive safe to glance at, and restore everything when I’m done."
"Tell me if anything the hive did recently may have leaked a secret, and show me exactly where so I can clean it up."
"What exactly happened between my button press and that browser change? Give me the timeline, the evidence, and what was not observed."
Read the page I mean in Safari and give me a trustworthy answer, even if the first extraction fails.
Start this multi-step job on my Mac and keep going until it is finished, even if the agent or link restarts; tell me exactly what was completed and what remains.
Why did that Mac or browser task fail, and what is the safest concrete next attempt?
Take the attachment from the email or web page I mean, verify what it is, place it in the correct project folder, and tell me exactly where it went and what it contains.
Find the issue or failed check in my authenticated developer tools, reproduce it in the matching local project, and give me a minimal evidence-backed fix plan without changing code unless I ask.
Since the last time I worked on this project, tell me what changed across the local checkout and its authenticated issue/PR pages, what is unfinished, and what I should do next.
Run this command and keep me updated on the pendant: tell me when it starts, read the meaningful progress as it happens, and let my next button press cancel it.
If my Mac went to sleep or restarted while doing something for me, tell me exactly what finished, what did not, and safely continue only the unfinished steps when I say 'resume'.
Take the thing I am looking at in Safari, do the necessary download or command-line processing on my Mac, and give me a spoken answer with links to the exact files and source page.
When I leave my Mac, pause any in-progress AI work that could expose private browser or file data, lock the Mac, and resume only when I am back and explicitly say 'continue' through the pendant.
At the start of my day, tell me what changed in the projects and web work I touched yesterday, what is still unresolved, and give me the exact evidence without rereading everything.
"Run this Mac task, and keep me informed until I know whether it really finished—even if the Mac or link drops."
"Save a receipt for this task that lets me or another agent reproduce exactly what happened on my Mac."
"Pick up where I left off."
"I’m about to close the lid—tell me what I’d lose, and leave everything in a state I can resume tomorrow."
"My Mac may be compromised or lost. Lock down my digital life now, and tell me exactly what you managed to revoke."
"Find the exact thing I was looking at or talking about yesterday, and open the source—not a guess."
“I changed something by accident—tell me exactly what the pendant just caused, and put it back if it is safely reversible.”
“Watch this authenticated browser page for a real change, and tell me only when the change is worth my attention.”
“While I was away, tell me which things you tried, which actually changed anything, and what still needs my attention.”
“Read the private page I’m looking at, but only speak it when you can prove the answer is going to my ears—not the room—and otherwise show me a silent confirmation.”
“Do that Mac task, and if it fails, keep trying safely until it either succeeds or tell me exactly what stopped it.”
“Stop the thing running on my Mac right now.”
“When I press the pendant button while it is plugged into my Mac, run my configured ‘focus’ routine and tell me what it changed—even if the relay is offline.”
“Start this work on my Mac, let me leave, and keep me updated through the pendant; if the browser or Mac becomes unavailable, pause at the exact step and resume when it returns.”
“Why are you telling me that—what did you actually see, and what did you infer?”
“Before I send this, tell me exactly what private information is leaving my Mac and where it is going.”
"Make the pendant sound wideband, and tell me if the link is degrading."
"When the pendant or Mac breaks, file a useful bug report and tell me what failed."

Add a global owner setting and policy that automatically manages the mac-vision agent's interaction frequency and confirmation depth based on task criticality and owner presence, reducing unnecessary interruptions while retaining safety for destructive actions.
“Summarize what I missed in my email today.”
entries.note: briefing.js kind=mail, reachable as 'Summarize what I missed in my email today.' Deterministic route, 24h-bounded Mail query, separates priority mail from newsletters. Live output: 'Good morning. 3 unread emails, all newsletters.'

entries.summary: “Read my upcoming schedule for the day.”
entries.note: briefing.js kind=schedule, reachable as 'Read my upcoming schedule for the day.' Deterministic route, renders long-form audio. Live output: 'Good morning. 7 meetings today, next is stand up at 9:00 AM. 2 need preparation.'

entries.summary: “Save this idea for later.”
entries.note: quickCapture.js: 'save this idea for later' parses off the lead-in and stores the idea whole. Two stores by design — memoryService (prompt tier, sensitivity-aware) and contextGraph (durable archive) — so an idea neither expires nor leaks. POST /capture, GET /capture?query=, action type quick_capture. 12 tests.

entries.summary: “Plan my day. Pull my calendar, summarize critical tasks and travel time, and give me a 30-second briefing.”
entries.note: dayPlan.js. Calendar+Reminders read through EventKit (appleData.js) because Calendar.app's AppleScript walks all 16 calendars per query. Briefing is built against a spoken word budget and drops whole sentences, never mid-sentence. Travel is the real gap between real places — a Zoom URL is not somewhere you travel to. Verified live: 3 events, 25 tasks, 48 words / ~17s inside a 30s target. GET /day-plan. 9 tests.

entries.summary: “Read my notifications and tell me only what’s important.”
entries.note: notificationTriage.js. Notification Center's DB needs Full Disk Access and logs dismissed banners anyway, so it triages the three sources that generate the interruptions: unread mail, imminent meetings, overdue reminders. Default is silence — everything must earn a threshold. Verified live: scanned 83, surfaced 2 past-due, suppressed 80, in 4.3s. 10 tests.

entries.summary: “Start a focus session for 25 minutes. Block distractions and let me know when time’s up.”
entries.note: focusSession.js. End time written to disk before anything is blocked, so the alarm survives a restart (resumeFocusSessions re-arms, or fires late rather than dropping). Blocking hides apps reversibly and restores only what this session changed. Verified live: hid Mail+Spotify in 0.6s, auto-ended at 2 min, spoke the alarm, restored both. 9 tests.

entries.summary: “Remember this: my bike lock code is 4829.”
entries.note: Same module. 'my X is Y' becomes a keyed fact; a spoken lock code is classified secret by new patterns in redaction.js, so the value lives in exactly one 0600 file and contextProjection renders it 'bike lock code: [withheld]' in prompts while the owner reads 4829 back in full. Verified live: 0 occurrences in context_graph.json, 1 in facts.json.

entries.summary: “Summarize the key points from this page and read them to me later.”
entries.note: mode=page: readOpenTabs() drives browser_list_tabs + browser_read_page over POST /execute, so pages are read in the owner's real logged-in profile, then summarized into key points and rendered to audio they play later. Falls back to the public web when no tab matches rather than failing. Verified live against open Safari tabs (2 tabs read, 78.6 s of audio).

entries.summary: "Summarize this webpage" or "Check the price on this product"
entries.note: Same capability and same code path as cap-d9af189b (mode=page): read the page the owner already has open and summarize it. Immediate delivery is the --now flag on the same command; price-on-this-product is that summary of the open product page. No separate implementation.

entries.summary: "Remind me to do X at 6 pm" or "Every weekday at 9, remind me to stand up"
entries.note: remindMe.js. One-off -> Apple Reminders (reused reminders.js, not a second path). Recurring -> a repeating Calendar event with an alarm, because routines.js cannot express 'not on Saturday' and only fires while the agent is up. Verified live: real Reminders item due Fri 18:00, real event 'stand up' FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,TU,WE,TH,FR at 09:00 with 1 alarm. 9 tests.

entries.summary: “Check the weather and read the highlights to me.”
entries.note: Already built, outside the briefing family: policyRouter.js has a get_weather deterministic matcher (no model call), computerControl dispatches it to local-agent/builtins/weather.js, which fetches wttr.in and returns a one-line current-conditions summary that pendantSpeech.js reads aloud. That is the whole ask as stated. Worth naming the ceiling rather than reopening it: wttr.in format=3 is one line of CURRENT conditions, so 'the highlights' is today's weather, not a multi-day forecast or a set of ranked alerts. Also noted on cap-c071fa0a: weather is a standalone action and is NOT folded into briefing.js's morning brief.

entries.summary: “When I get back to my desk, summarize what happened while I was away and queue anything urgent.”
entries.note: "When I get back to my desk, summarize what happened while I was away" is now the deferral path in cloud-relay/routines.js. A routine that needs the Mac (calendar, mail, notes, files, screen) and comes due while the lid is closed is NOT failed and NOT faked by the relay: chooseVenue returns 'defer', the occurrence is held with its original dueAt and retried each minute, and it runs the moment the bridge heartbeat returns — then its answer becomes a spoken announcement. Bounded at 12 h so a long absence drops the occurrence with a 'missed' receipt instead of firing a pile of stale briefings at once. Verified live: Mac-venue routine dispatched, the bridge ran it, reapDispatchedRuns turned the result into a pending announcement.

entries.summary: “Remind me every weekday at 5 to shut down and summarize what I did today.”
entries.note: "Remind me every weekday at 5" is expressible and durable: {kind:'weekly', at:'17:00', days:['weekdays']} in cloud-relay/routineSchedule.js, with an IANA timezone because a Worker runs in UTC and a naive setHours(17) would fire at 11am Central. DST-stable (two-pass offset resolution, tested across the 2026-11-01 transition). The summarize half runs on the Mac when it is awake and defers when it is not (cap-64c3562b). Reaching the pendant unprompted at 5pm still needs firmware — see the README section 'How an announcement reaches the pendant'; today the brief is spoken the moment the next press opens the socket.

Verified live in this round: it returned two past-due reminders and suppressed 80 other items.

“I asked you to handle that on my Mac—what’s the status?”
entries.note: Shipped as the relay_job_status Realtime tool (7th tool in REALTIME_TOOLS), backed by the new cloud-relay/jobRecall.js. Note was empty before this; nothing to preserve. Voice path end to end: openaiRealtimeVoice.js answers the tool INSIDE the turn like web_search — it never sets state.actions, so a status question dispatches no Mac job — and both session call sites inject the lookup (cloud-relay/server.js /v1/pendant/command, cloud-relay/pendantConverse.js duplex WS). SOURCE: relay job records via store.listJobs({type:'plan'}), not the Mac journal. Deliberate: the relay already holds the Mac's returned result/error for every job it dispatched, it is in-process (no round trip inside a spoken turn), and it still answers when the Mac is asleep — which is exactly the case where 'your Mac never picked it up' is the true answer. local-agent /journal is richer per action but needs a live bridge round trip and is not in OPS_ALLOWED_PREFIXES. REFERENCE HEURISTIC: explicit jobId wins; only type='plan' jobs are candidates (agent_proxy is plumbing, audio_capture is a spoken reply with no Mac work); deictics and status-question scaffolding are stripped to nothing before scoring so 'that'/'the thing I asked earlier' contribute zero evidence; content overlap x10 dominates recency; recency+unfinished only break ties; a reference that DID name something but matched nothing resolves to nothing rather than falling back to the newest job; with no content words, candidates older than 30 min are dropped; near-ties are flagged ambiguous and the spoken line always NAMES the task so a wrong pick is correctable in the next breath. HONESTY: describeJobOutcome is the single place that decides success. Terminal status with no result => 'unknown', and executed:false => 'failed' — the voiceRunForCapture bug (hardcoded success, silent runs reported completed) is covered by two regression tests. Approval gates report as awaiting_approval; queued past 60s reports as 'your Mac hasn't picked it up'. No approval gates or confirmation prompts added. SPOKEN: one sentence, hard-capped at 180 chars (same clip bridge.js uses), relative times ('3 minutes ago'), never JSON. TESTS: 21 in cloud-relay/jobRecall.test.js + 1 schema test in openaiRealtimeVoice.test.js. Two drift guards updated six->seven: openaiRealtimeVoice.test.js and local-agent/stackAlignment.test.js. Full suite green (832/832). NOT VERIFIED: no live OpenAI Realtime turn was run (needs an API key and the pendant), and the live Mac agent's job store is token-gated so real owner jobs were not read; the real query was run against the real cloud-relay in-memory store through the exact lookupJobStatus closure. Worker not deployed.
